title: Conduction App Manifest v2
description: v2 schema for the JSON-driven page and navigation manifest consumed by @conduction/nextcloud-vue. Introduces a uniform widgets[] array on every page type with a per-slot grid coordinate system, a typed actions[] discriminator, and the required $schema field for version detection. v1 manifests continue to validate against app-manifest.schema.json (unchanged).

allOf.$comment: UI manifests: a manifest that declares pages MUST also declare menu (unchanged v2 coupling).

Observability-only profile: a manifest with no pages MUST carry an observability block. ADR-040 Tier-0 adopters (e.g. nldesign, planix) ship src/manifest.json solely as AppHost engine config — the app renders no manifest-driven UI, so forcing menu/pages on them produced permanently-failing gate-22 manifests (2026-07-06 fleet audit, item 3b).

$schema.description: REQUIRED in v2. Must point to the v2 schema URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ConductionNL/nextcloud-vue/main/src/schemas/app-manifest-v2.schema.json. Presence of this field enables the validator to dispatch to the v2 Ajv instance rather than the v1 hand-rolled validator.

version.description: Semver of the manifest content. Bump when the manifest changes meaningfully. Used for cache busting and app-builder migration tracking. Distinct from the schema's own version.

openbuildEditable.description: Whether the Buildiq in-app edit button (ADR-041) is offered on this app's pages. Default true. Set false to suppress it — e.g. Buildiq's own UI, which does not edit itself with itself. Read by CnAppRoot to gate `cnOpenBuildAvailable`. The property name and the inject key keep their `openbuild` spelling: both are data/runtime contracts that shipped manifests and consumer apps already carry, so the 2026-08-21 OpenBuild → Buildiq rename deliberately left them untouched.

id.description: Nextcloud app id.

required.description: true (default) = HARD: absence blocks the app shell behind CnDependencyMissing. false = SOFT: an optional integration whose absence surfaces a dismissible in-shell notice and never blocks.

name.description: Human-readable display label; falls back to id.

dependencies.description: Nextcloud app dependencies. Each entry is either a string (a HARD dependency — the app cannot run without it, absence blocks the shell) or an object { id, required?, name? } where required:false marks a SOFT (optional) dependency (required defaults to true). CnAppRoot checks each via useAppStatus(id); unresolved HARD deps block behind CnDependencyMissing, unresolved SOFT deps show a dismissible NcNoteCard banner. Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed here — resolved at build time against known app IDs.

setup.description: First-time setup wizard (ADR-042). Rendered by CnSetupWizard; required steps gate the app via CnAppRoot's setup phase. Steps run privileged server-side actions via /api/setup/action — the wizard never writes OpenRegister objects from the browser.

enabled.description: Whether the setup wizard is active for this app.

version.description: Setup contract version; bump to re-trigger setup after a breaking change.

completionConfigKey.description: App-config key storing the completed setup version.

dismissAction.description: Setup action that records a closed or finished setup wizard on the server, so it stays closed in every browser. CnAppRoot posts `/apps/{appId}/api/setup/action/{dismissAction}` with `{ finished }` once when the user closes or finishes the wizard. The app either answers the outstanding optional steps or reports `dismissed` (true, or the setup version it was closed at) in `GET /api/setup/status`. Without it, the close is remembered only in the browser (localStorage), as before.

steps.description: Ordered setup steps rendered by CnSetupWizard.

id.description: Unique step id; also the #step-<id> slot name.

required.description: When true the step gates the app until done.

schema.description: config-fields: a JSON Schema ref (string) or inline object rendered via fieldsFromSchema.

configKey.description: choice: app-config key the selection is written to.

configKeys.description: config-fields: app-config keys the fields write.

optionsSource.description: choice: where to read the option list from at runtime, instead of declaring it here. Names a key in the app's own GET /api/setup/status document (dots walk into nested objects, e.g. `profiles`). Entries accept `id` for `value` and `name` for `label`, and a numeric `objectCount` becomes the stat a card shows. Use it when the SERVER owns what is on offer, so the manifest cannot drift from it.

display.description: choice: how the options are rendered. `select` is a dropdown; `cards` is a grid of CnChoiceCards, which shows each option's description and stats. Pick cards when the choice needs explaining.

dependsOn.description: choice: the configKey of a previous choice step this one cascades from. Disabled until the parent is set; its option list is taken from optionsByParent[parentValue] (e.g. organisation-type depends on country).

optionsByParent.description: choice: map of parent-choice value → options[] for a dependent (dependsOn) choice. Same option item shape as `options`.

suggestFrom.description: choice: the configKey of an earlier choice this step pre-fills a suggestion from. When that value is set and the user has not yet picked here, the option matching suggestMap[parentValue] is auto-selected (still user-overridable).

suggestMap.description: choice: map of suggestFrom value → suggested option value. Used to auto-suggest a default (e.g. RGS template suggested from organisation type).

loadAction.description: choice with display cards: an actionId each option card loads itself with. Every card except the one whose value is `none` gets its own Load button, which POSTs { dataset: <value> } to /api/setup/action/{loadAction}, spins while it runs and shows the result on that card. A successful load also selects the card. With loadAction the separate run-action step that loaded the picked dataset is no longer needed; manifests that keep it still work.

requires.description: App ids this step needs. When any of them is not installed and enabled, the wizard skips the step and the summary shows it as skipped, naming the missing apps. Setup status then counts the step as not applicable, neither met nor unmet, so it never reopens the wizard or gates the app. This holds for a required step too.

onDemand.description: run-action: the step runs only when the user clicks Run, never automatically, and is never outstanding work (it does not open the wizard or decide where a resumed wizard starts). The summary ticks it only when its action succeeded in the current session and shows it as not run otherwise, whatever the server reports. For destructive steps an app reports as done on purpose so they never auto-run, such as removing example data.

component.description: component: app-registered component name (or use the #step-<id> slot).

walkthrough.description: Abstract product walkthrough (ADR-043). One or more spotlighted, versioned tours rendered by CnWalkthrough over the live shell.

enabled.description: Master switch; when false no tour auto-starts.

completionConfigKey.description: Per-user app-config key holding the last app version whose tour the user has seen.

id.description: Unique tour id (globally unique for cross-app hand-off, e.g. 'pipelinq:lead-to-bill').

title.description: i18n key / text for the tour name (restart menu).

minAppVersion.description: Semver; the tour is inert below this app version.

id.description: Unique step id within the tour.

title.description: i18n key / text for the coachmark title.

body.description: i18n key / text for the coachmark body; supports {{contextVar}} interpolation.

task.description: Optional 'go do this' instruction; presence + a non-manual advanceOn makes this an enforced action step.

sinceVersion.description: Semver the step was introduced in; drives the 'what's new' composition.

placement.description: Coachmark placement; 'center' renders anchorless with no cutout.

optional.description: Skip gracefully when the target/condition is absent.

allowManualNext.description: Show a manual Next escape hatch on an enforced action step.

handoff.description: Cross-app hand-off (ADR-043). When present, the coachmark primary action becomes 'Continue in {app}' and navigates to `url` carrying a cn_resume_tour/cn_resume_step token so the destination app resumes the named tour.

tour.description: Tour id to resume in the destination (defaults to this tour's id).

step.description: Step id to resume at (defaults to the destination tour's first step).

ref.description: Stable id: route name (nav-item/page), widgetKey (widget), action id (action), or data-walkthrough-id / data-testid (element).

app.description: Optional other Conduction app id for a cross-app target (page kind).

selector.description: Raw CSS selector for kind:selector (last resort).

route.description: route-match: the route name to await.

capture.description: Map of contextVar -> ':param' (route-match) or ':id' (object-created) captured into the tour context for {{var}} interpolation.

support.description: First-open support and donation note. CnAppRoot mounts CnSupportDialog once per user on first open and reads this block; CnEditSupportModal edits it. Omitting the block keeps the default-on behaviour with the shell's own copy, so an app only declares what it wants to override. The block was read by CnAppRoot and written by CnEditSupportModal before it was declared here, which made `additionalProperties: false` reject every manifest that set it.

enabled.description: Whether the note is shown on first open. Omit for the default (true); set false to suppress it for this app.

title.description: Dialog heading. Blank keeps the shell default.

appName.description: Display name interpolated into the body copy. Defaults to the host app's name.

bodyParagraphs.description: Body copy, one entry per paragraph, replacing the shell's default paragraphs.

founderTitle.description: Signature role, shown under the name.

founderProfileUrl.description: Profile the signature avatar links to.

buttons.description: Per-button overrides, keyed by the four built-in button ids. Each may be hidden, relabelled, restyled or re-pointed; omit a key to keep its default.

personalisation.description: App defaults for the per-user options CnPersonalPreferences renders, and the switch that turns the personal layer off instance wide.

includePersonalSettings.description: Auto-prepend a 'Personal settings' entry at the top of the settings foldout (opens the host's NcAppSettingsDialog via cnOpenUserSettings). Set false for apps with no per-user settings.

settingsLabel.description: Override label for the settings foldout's gear button. Defaults to 'Advanced'.

card.description: A card above the footer entries, rendered by CnAppNav (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps): a title, a line of text and one link. Title, text and link label are i18n keys. Omitted, nothing renders there.

link.description: The card's link: a `route` (named page, optional `params`) is a router link, an `href` a plain anchor, an `action` id a button that emits `card-action`.

help.description: A help entry with a help icon in the navigation footer, above the settings foldout (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps): `route` (named page) or `href` (opens in a new tab).

footer.description: Declare the navigation footer (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-2): an ordered list of `section: "footer"` menu entry ids, plus the reserved ids `help` (the `nav.help` entry) and `settings` (the settings foldout). Only the named footer entries render there, in that order; footer entries left out move into the settings foldout so their pages stay reachable. `settings` first puts the foldout above the list (the board's `["settings", "help"]`). Omitted, the footer renders as before: help, every footer entry, then the foldout.

primaryAction.description: App-wide default primary action rendered as an NcAppNavigationNew button above the main menu list. A page-scoped pages[].primaryAction for the current route wins over this default.

brand.description: A brand block at the very top of the app navigation, above the primary action: a logo, a name and a caption. Rendered by CnAppNav. Omitted, nothing renders there.

logo.description: URL of the logo image. Decorative when `name` is set.

emblem.description: An emblem drawn in place of the logo (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps): the municipality's mark beside the app name, distinct from the wordmark in the top bar. A URL, or `true` to draw the theme's emblem from the `--nldesign-emblem-url` custom property. Decorative when `name` is set.

name.description: i18n key / text for the app or organisation name.

caption.description: i18n key / text for the line under the name, for example the organisation.

alt.description: i18n key / alternative text for the logo. Used only when no `name` is set.

featureRequestRepo.description: `<owner>/<repo>` slug on the forge that the in-product feature-request deep-link targets (provided to descendants as `cnFeatureRequestRepo`). Falls back to `Conduction/<appId>` when omitted.

forge.description: Forge that the in-product feature-request deep-link targets. Switching the whole fleet's forge (onto a self-hosted Forgejo/Gitea, or back to Codeberg) is just this one field. Defaults to GitHub, the only host the fleet publishes to.

type.description: Forge type. Selects how the 'new issue' form is pre-filled: `github` uses per-field Issue-Form query params; `codeberg`/`forgejo`/`gitea` assemble a Markdown body (only title + body are supported there).

baseUrl.description: Override the forge host. Required for self-hosted `forgejo`/`gitea`; optional for `codeberg`/`github` (their canonical public hosts are used when omitted).

runtime.description: Runtime context data injected into the manifest by the backend (e.g. OpenRegister) at serve time. Carries per-user fields that visibleIf context-path predicates resolve against. The canonical sub-object is 'user', which exposes user-specific flags and role information.

user.description: Per-user runtime context. Populated by the backend for authenticated requests. All fields are optional; the FE predicate evaluator treats missing fields as undefined.

theme.description: NL Design System scoped theme selection (scoped-theme-applier). Consumed by CnAppRoot's useScopedTheme wiring, not by the backend.

menu.description: Top-level navigation entries rendered by CnAppNav.

pages.description: Page definitions dispatched by CnPageRenderer. Each page's id is also its vue-router route name. Ids MUST be unique across the array; uniqueness is enforced by validateManifestV2 as a post-schema check.

adminSettings.description: Admin-only settings sections rendered by CnAppRoot's generic admin NcAppSettingsDialog, gated on app-owner-group membership (not OC.isUserAdmin()). An absent key or an empty array yields no admin nav entry and no admin dialog. See the manifest-admin-settings and admin-settings-owner-gating capabilities.

credentials.description: External-provider credentials this app can use via the OpenRegister credential broker (github, gitlab, …). Each entry declares which provider, why, and at what scope; the app never receives the secret — the broker performs the outbound call on the user's behalf. See the credential-broker capability.

provider.description: Catalogue provider identifier (e.g. "github", "gitlab") — a key in OpenRegister's credential-providers catalogue.

reason.description: Human-readable reason shown to the user in credential settings (why the app wants this provider).

schedules.description: Declarative scheduled tasks (apphost-scheduling capability). Each entry declares a recurring task the OpenRegister AppHost schedule-reconciler turns into an Integriq job that runs on the existing background-job path — so a manifest-driven app (including a pure-virtual Buildiq app with no PHP on disk) can own its ingestion/maintenance cadence without shipping a TimedJob. The temporal peer of `credentials`/`observability`: consumed by the OpenRegister engine, NOT by the Vue renderer. Optional and additive.

id.description: Stable identifier for this schedule, unique within the manifest. The reconciled job is keyed on applicationId + this id, so renaming it creates a new job and orphans the old one (which is then garbage-collected).

interval.description: Run cadence in seconds (e.g. 604800 = weekly). Exactly one of `interval` or `cron` must be set.

cron.description: Standard 5-field cron expression (e.g. "0 3 * * 1"). The reconciler computes the job's nextRun from it. Exactly one of `interval` or `cron` must be set.

action.description: A server-allow-listed generic action type, NOT a PHP class name. Only vetted types are accepted (v1: "openconnector:synchronization"); the reconciler maps the type to a trusted jobClass — a manifest-supplied class name is never executed. A non-allow-listed action is rejected and logged.

arguments.description: Free-form arguments passed to the action (e.g. the synchronization id/ref). Interpreted by the vetted action, not by the reconciler.

enabled.description: Whether this schedule is active. Defaults to true. Setting false disables the reconciled job (preserving its run history) rather than deleting it.

observability.description: Declarative observability block (ADR-040). Consumed at request time by the OpenRegister AppHost observability engine (GenericHealthController + GenericMetricsController), NOT by the Vue renderer. Declares the app's health checks and Prometheus metric descriptors so adopting apps ship zero hand-written observability PHP while keeping their /api/health + /api/metrics URLs and the ADR-006 contract.

store.description: ADR-080 / ADR-114 Decision 4. The declarative store plane. An app that declares this block gets a working Store surface with NO backend of its own: OpenRegister's AppHost aliases /api/store/items and /api/store/items/{slug}/install at its GenericStoreController, which reads this block at request time. Discovery stays in the engine (the SSRF guard, the redirect refusal and the registry token never leave it) and the app builds no registry URL.

anyOf.title: An objects store names the remote schema its registry serves.
A configuration store names the shareable types it surfaces.

schema.description: Remote schema slug the registry serves (e.g. "case-type-template", "application-template").

register.description: Remote register segment, used when the instance's registry_register config is unset or empty.

localRegister.description: The register an install WRITES into. Defaults to the app id. A schema slug is NOT unique across the fleet (`case`, `task` and `document` exist in several apps at once), so an unscoped write can land in another app's register: an app whose OpenRegister register slug differs from its app id must set this.

installable.description: Schema slugs an install may write. THIS IS A SECURITY BOUNDARY, not a convenience: a registry is somebody else's server, and without the allowlist an item could name any schema the app owns. An absent or empty list refuses EVERY install rather than permitting every install.

kinds.description: Kind quick-filters (ADR-080 Decision 5). Declared ONCE here, beside the allowlist: the engine returns them in the search response and CnStorePage prefers them over its page config. Defaults to the shared vocabulary when omitted.

types.description: Shareable configuration type ids this store surfaces (store-over-federated-config). Declaring these makes the store exchange CONFIGURATION rather than rows: an item is a configuration set (`openregister.configset`), a flow (`openregister.flows`), a register with its schemas (`openregister.registers`), or any schema that marked itself `x-openregister-shareable`. Cards come from federated discovery and an install runs through the owning type, so a set arrives as registers, schemas, objects, views, flows, sources and mappings. An app that declares none keeps the remote objects API described by `schema`/`register`, and makes no discovery call at all.

cardFields.description: Card field to remote property map. Defaults to the field names the fleet's registries already publish.

builtIn.description: The items this app ships itself, rendered when no registry is configured or the registry does not answer. ADR-080 Decision 4 makes this the price of the word Store: a surface that goes blank without a registry was never a store.

deepLinks.description: ADR-040: object deep-link descriptors consumed by the integration registry / cross-app linking, NOT by the Vue renderer. Optional and additive.

pageTemplates.description: Entity-scaffold page templates (manifest-entity-scaffold-templating). A template declares one reusable index/detail page shape ONCE, with `{{param}}` placeholders for the parts that vary per entity (register/schema binding, label, field/column subset) and a declared parameter list. The expander (utils/expandPageTemplates) materialises `pageInstances[]` into concrete `pages[]` at build/boot time, so CnPageRenderer only ever sees concrete pages and is unchanged by templating. Optional and additive: a manifest without pageTemplates is unaffected.

pageInstances.description: Per-entity template instantiations. Each entry references a `pageTemplates[]` template by `templateRef` and supplies only the values that vary. The expander substitutes them into the referenced template and appends the resulting concrete pages to `pages[]`. Expansion FAILS (named error) on an unknown templateRef or a missing required template parameter. Optional and additive.

sets.description: Named, reusable field/column/sidebar sets referenced from templates via a `{{set:NAME}}` placeholder, so a repeated field/column/sidebar block is declared ONCE and shared across templates and pages instead of being re-listed. Each value is arbitrary JSON (typically an array of field/column defs or a sidebar object). Optional and additive.

mcp.title: MCP tool visibility hints
mcp.description: OPTIONAL. Advisory visibility/UX hints for MCP tool surfaces (Hermiq agent tool picker, openbuild tool browser). Purely presentational: per ADR-063, OpenRegister's register (x-openregister-mcp dialect + #[McpTool] attributes) is the single source of CRUD-tool truth and OpenRegister RBAC is the authoritative invoke-time gate. This block grants no access and gates nothing; nothing in nextcloud-vue consumes it.

expose.title: App-level exposure hint
expose.description: Advisory app-wide default for whether this app's register-derived MCP tools should be shown in agent / tool-picker surfaces. Advisory only — the authoritative gate is OpenRegister RBAC plus per-agent whitelists. Defaults to false (opt-in), matching ADR-063's default-OFF exposure model.

pageTools.title: Per-page tool hints
pageTools.description: Maps a pages[].id to the ordered list of MCP tool ids that are contextually relevant on that page. Advisory grouping for UX surfaces only; it does not grant access. Keys are expected to match an existing pages[].id; the register remains authoritative for whether each listed tool actually exists.

additionalProperties.title: Relevant tool ids for a page
additionalProperties.description: Ordered MCP tool ids relevant to the page keyed above. Advisory ordering only.

items.title: MCP tool id
items.description: A fully-qualified MCP tool id in the register's derived-CRUD shape {appId}.{schemaSlug}.{verb}, verb one of search|get|create|update|delete (ADR-063). Example only: "pipelinq.lead.search". The register is authoritative for existence; this is a hint.

agentHints.title: Agent-facing hints
agentHints.description: Advisory metadata for agent surfaces (Hermiq). All values are non-authoritative UX hints. Additional properties are permitted so consuming surfaces can introduce new advisory hints without a schema release (forward compatibility).

summary.title: App tool summary
summary.description: One-line description of what this app's tools help an agent accomplish. Shown in agent / tool-picker surfaces.

defaultTools.title: Default tool ids
defaultTools.description: MCP tool ids to surface first / preselect when an agent has no page context. Advisory ordering hint only; not a grant.

items.title: MCP tool id
items.description: Fully-qualified MCP tool id {appId}.{schemaSlug}.{verb}. Example only: "pipelinq.lead.search".

keywords.title: Discovery keywords
keywords.description: Keywords helping progressive-disclosure / tool-search surfaces (Hermiq) rank this app's tools. Advisory only.

rowIndicator.description: One declared state indicator on an index page's rows. Renders as an icon with a text alternative and a tooltip, never as colour alone.

id.description: Stable id for this indicator, used as its test id and its render key. Defaults to `field`.

field.description: Dotted path on the row the condition reads.

equals.description: The indicator applies when the field equals this value exactly.

in.description: The indicator applies when the field's value is one of these.

text.description: The text alternative, read out beside the icon. Required: an indicator without one does not render.

folderSidebarScope.description: One folder in `config.folderSidebar.folders[]`, which doubles as a SCOPE: the three optional list-layout keys below let one index page show each folder the way that folder needs. Every other key (id, name, icon, ...) stays free-form, so an existing folder list validates unchanged. The page's `config.columns` still decides which columns this page HAS; a scope only decides which of them are shown, in what order, sorted by what and searched over what. A scope naming a column the page does not declare is refused by validateManifestV2, not silently rendered.

columns.description: The columns this scope shows, in order. Same shapes as `config.columns`: a bare key string or a column object. Every key must be one the page's `config.columns` declares. Omit to show the page's own columns.

defaultSort.description: The sort the fetch carries while this scope is active. One `{ key, order }` entry or a list of them; `order` is 'asc' (default) or 'desc'. `field` is accepted in place of `key`, matching the CnIndexPage `defaultSort` prop.

searchFields.description: The fields the search box searches over while this scope is active. Omit to search whatever the page searches by default.

folderSidebarScopeSort.description: One sort entry for a `folderSidebar` scope. Name the column with `key` (manifest spelling) or `field` (the CnIndexPage prop spelling); an entry carrying neither is dropped rather than sent as an empty sort key.

supportButton.description: Override for one of the four built-in support-note buttons (donate, support, feature-request, app-store). Every field is optional; omit the whole entry to keep the shell's default for that button.

enabled.description: Show this button. Set false to hide it.

label.description: Button text. Blank keeps the default label.

url.description: Where the button goes. The feature-request and app-store buttons have no useful default, so an app that wants them must set this.

icon.description: Material Design Icon component name, e.g. HeartOutline.

runtimeTheme.description: A leaf app's NL Design token-set selection, as returned by nldesign's GET /api/token-sets catalogue (app-token-set-selection). Applied by CnAppRoot via useScopedTheme — the ONLY consumer; the backend does not read this field.

source.description: Theme provider. Closed to 'nldesign' — the only scoped-theme source this schema (and useScopedTheme) currently supports.

tokenSet.description: The nldesign token-set id (a GET /api/token-sets entry's `id`), kebab-case. Resolves the token CSS at css/tokens/<tokenSet>.css.

tokenSetName.description: Optional human-readable name (the matching catalogue entry's `name`), cached at selection time so a picker can display it without a second catalogue fetch.

preview.description: Optional cached swatch preview (the matching catalogue entry's theming colors), for a picker to render a preview chip without re-fetching the catalogue.

primaryColor.description: Cached theming.primary_color from the catalogue entry.

backgroundColor.description: Cached theming.background_color from the catalogue entry.

pageTemplate.description: A reusable page shape declared once and instantiated per entity. `page` is an ordinary v2 page object whose string values may contain `{{param}}` placeholders (and `{{set:NAME}}` set references); `params` declares which placeholders exist and which are required. Fixed structure lives in `page`; only declared params vary per instantiation.

id.description: Unique template identifier — the `templateRef` target. Uniqueness across pageTemplates[] is enforced by validateManifestV2 as a post-schema check.

_note.description: Free-form maintainer note; ignored by the expander.

params.description: Declared parameters. A placeholder `{{name}}` in `page` is substituted with the instantiation's value for `name`. A `required` param absent from an instantiation is an expansion error; an optional param absent from an instantiation causes its exact-match placeholder key to be omitted from the expanded page.

name.description: Parameter name, referenced as `{{name}}` in the template `page`.

required.description: When true, an instantiation omitting this parameter is an expansion error.

page.description: The parameterised page shape. An ordinary v2 page whose string leaves may embed `{{param}}` placeholders and `{{set:NAME}}` set references. After substitution the result MUST be a valid concrete page (it is validated as part of the expanded pages[]).

pageInstance.description: A per-entity instantiation of a pageTemplate. Supplies only the values that vary. `register`, `schema` and `label` are first-class shortcuts folded into the parameter map (equivalent to listing them under `params`); `params` may carry any additional declared parameters (e.g. a field/column subset).

templateRef.description: Id of the `pageTemplates[]` entry to instantiate. An unknown templateRef is an expansion error.

params.description: Parameter values keyed by the template's declared parameter names. Values may be any JSON type (a field/column subset is an array value). Overrides the register/schema/label shortcuts on conflict.

override.description: Optional structural delta applied over the substituted page via the SAME base+delta merge semantics as mergeManifestDelta (layered-versioned-app-deltas alignment). Lets an instantiation patch a single widget/field without re-listing the page, and is where a per-user/app override sits on top of the template base. No second merge model is introduced.

sentinelFilterToken.description: Filter-value context: relative fetch-time tokens resolved by resolveFilterTokens (@me, @now, @today, @today±Nd, @monthStart, @quarterStart, @yearStart). Mirrors SENTINEL_TOKEN_PATTERNS.filter in src/utils/sentinelTokens.js (byte-equality enforced by a unit test).

sentinelConfigToken.description: Config context: IAppConfig-sourced values. @resolve:<key> resolved at manifest-load time; @config.<key> (trailing ? optional) at fetch time. Mirrors SENTINEL_TOKEN_PATTERNS.config.

sentinelObjectToken.description: Object context: detail-page object tokens (@objectId, @object.<field>) resolved only when a { objectId, object } ctx is supplied. Mirrors SENTINEL_TOKEN_PATTERNS.object.

sentinelWorkspaceToken.description: Workspace context: page-level workspace state (@workspace.<key>; trailing ? marks optional). Mirrors SENTINEL_TOKEN_PATTERNS.workspace.

sentinelRouteToken.description: Route context: vue-router param substitution (@route.<param>) resolved by resolveRouteSentinels. Mirrors SENTINEL_TOKEN_PATTERNS.route.

sentinelDeclarativeToken.description: Declarative context (OpenRegister direction, resolved server-side): @self.<field> (the object's own field in a cross-object calc), @ref:<path>, @aggregate:<expr>. @ref/@aggregate are first-class members even though currently unused fleet-wide. Mirrors SENTINEL_TOKEN_PATTERNS.declarative.

sentinelDeprecatedToken.description: Deprecated single-app inventions kept in the union so deployed manifests still validate during the migration window. The hydra token-vocabulary gate downgrades these to a WARN (see SENTINEL_DEPRECATIONS): @currentFiscalYear → @config.fiscalYear, @page.<key> → @workspace.<key>, @runtime → removal. Mirrors SENTINEL_TOKEN_PATTERNS.deprecated.

sentinelVisibleWhenToken.description: manifest-form-logic: the shared visibleWhen predicate's source-mode collection-total marker, resolved client-side by evaluateVisibleWhen (utils/visibleWhen.js) — NOT one of the four IAppConfig/OpenRegister resolvers, but a pre-existing convention (already documented on $defs.visibleWhen and the banner widget) reachable through the sentinelGuardedValue-guarded pages[].config subtree for the first time via config.fields[].visibleWhen. Mirrors SENTINEL_TOKEN_PATTERNS.visibleWhen.

sentinelTokenAny.$comment: Union of every canonical context plus the deprecated-during-window overlay. Single source the shared resolver + gate import.

sentinelTokenLeaf.$comment: A string leaf: either NOT a sentinel (does not start with @) or a member of the closed vocabulary. An @-prefixed out-of-vocabulary string FAILS here instead of passing through additionalProperties:true.

sentinelGuardedValue.$comment: Recursive guard applied (via allOf) to pages[].config and widgetEntry so every string leaf anywhere beneath is checked against the closed vocabulary. Additive + backward-compatible: only @-prefixed out-of-vocabulary strings newly fail; all other shapes are untouched.

observability.description: Health checks + metric descriptors executed by the AppHost engine.

_note.description: Free-form note for maintainers; ignored by the engine.

health.description: Declarative health checks rendered as the ADR-006 {status, app, version, checks} shape.

statusCodePolicy.description: HTTP status-code policy. 'adr006' returns 503 on a failed critical check; 'always200' always returns 200.

id.description: Check id, surfaced as the key in the response's checks map.

severity.description: critical → a failure flips status to error (503 under adr006); degraded → status degraded (200).

app.description: App id, for the appEnabled check.

key.description: Config key, for the appConfig check.

cors.description: ADR-040: when true the engine emits permissive CORS headers on the /api/health response.

metrics.description: Prometheus metric descriptors. The {app}_ prefix, exposition format, and implicit {app}_info / {app}_up gauges are engine-owned.

name.description: Metric name (without the {app}_ prefix the engine adds).

help.description: HELP text for the metric family.

cacheTtl.description: ADR-040: optional per-metric cache TTL in seconds.

source.description: Where the engine sources the value.

kind.description: Source kind. tableCount = COUNT over an allowlisted own-table; objectCount = OR objects by register/schema; appConfig = a numeric app-config value; provider = an IMetricsProvider implementation.

field.description: objectSum: the numeric object property to SUM.

groupBy.description: Columns to GROUP BY (one label per column).

labelMap.description: Rename a groupBy column to a different Prometheus label name.

labelDefaults.description: Default label value for NULL/empty group columns.

key.description: appConfig: the config key whose numeric value is the sample.

id.description: provider: the IMetricsProvider id to invoke.

splitView.description: The list and one open record, side by side. Declared on an index page; buildManifestRoutes() then emits a second route <route>/split/:id under the name <pageId>__split, carrying meta.cnSplitOf so CnPageRenderer still resolves it to this page and the list never unmounts.

enabled.description: Whether opening a row opens it beside the list. False renders exactly as today: a full page list and a full page detail.

breakpoint.description: Viewport width in pixels below which the split address renders the full detail page instead of the pane, so a link sent from a laptop opens on a phone.

paneWidth.description: CSS width of the detail pane, e.g. '38%' or '520px'. Defaults to '42%'.

savedViewTree.description: Saved views render as a tree rather than a flat list, carry labels, and may ship with the app. Two hundred personal views in one dropdown is the problem this solves. Index pages only, and only meaningful alongside allowSavedViews: without the dropdown there is no view to put in a tree. Absent, the page renders the flat dropdown it renders today. The view entity itself, its parent, its labels and its slug are OpenRegister's (saved-search-views); this key declares how this page presents them.

enabled.description: Whether this page renders its saved views as a tree. False reads as a page that considered it and declined, and renders exactly as a page that never named the key.

maxDepth.description: How deep a parent chain may go. A bound rather than a taste: inheritance resolves by walking the chain, so an unbounded depth turns one render into an unbounded walk, and a person who can nest for ever will. Past the bound a save is refused naming the view, which is louder than a tree nobody can read.

templates.description: What a new view may start from. A template presets the columns, the sort and the export field set, and the person may change each. Declare none and Save current view means what it has always meant: the list as it stands.

landingView.description: Which view a role opens this page on, as { role: slug }. A personal choice always wins and Reset returns here, so this is where somebody starts rather than where they are kept. A role's landing view changing mid-session applies on the next arrival: moving a reader's list out from under them is worse than a stale default.

columnsPerRole.description: Which columns a role sees, as { role: [column] }. NARROWS index-columns-per-scope rather than replacing it: a role naming a column the scope does not offer gets nothing extra, because a per-role list that could add one would be a second, quieter way to put a field on screen the scope deliberately left off.

groupBy.description: A field the list groups on, with a count per group. The counts are of the rows the list HOLDS, so on a paged list they are of the page and the surface says so; a second fetch per group is the cost this grouping exists to avoid.

seeded.description: Views that ship with the app. They render as their own group above the user's own, and a user may copy one but not delete it: a view the product promises is not a view one person can remove from everybody's install.

slug.description: The stable name a dashboard widget, an export action or an API caller cites this view by. Lowercase and dash only, because it appears in an address and in a manifest somebody else writes. Required: a seeded view with no slug is a view nothing can call, which is most of the reason to seed it.

name.description: What the view is called in the control. Translatable.

label.description: One label this view carries, for the label filter. A view may carry none and stays reachable when no label filter is active.

parent.description: The slug of the view this one hangs under. Omitted, it sits at the root of the seeded group.

actions.description: The action ids this view offers, so a triage view offers three and not thirty. INTERSECTED with what the reader may run and never added to: a view declaring an action the reader has no right to does not grant it. Declare none and the view offers the page's actions, as today.

inherits.description: Which parts this view takes from its parent. Each part resolves independently, so a child may narrow the criteria and keep the parent's columns. Declared on a view with no parent it is a contradiction and the validator refuses it: there is nothing to inherit from.

allOf.description: inherits without a parent is a declaration that reads as configured and resolves to nothing. Refused here rather than silently ignored at render, which is the shape this whole change exists to stop.

boardView.description: The board view of this list: one column per stage of a status field. Index pages only, and only offered when `viewModes` also lists `board`. The COLUMNS COME FROM THE SCHEMA, not from the values present in the loaded rows: a board built from the data would lose the stage nothing is in, which is the one you drag a card into, and would reorder itself as work moved. A move goes through the host's transition and never writes the status field, so a board can never move a case past a rule the case page enforces.

statusField.description: The property the columns come from. Required: a board with no status field has nothing to be a board of. Its enum or lifecycle states are read from the register schema at RUNTIME, so a field with neither cannot be caught here; the view says so on screen instead of drawing empty columns.

cardFields.description: The fields a card shows. Keep it short: a card is scanned, not read.

swimlaneField.description: A second field to group the board into rows by, while the columns stay the stages. Cards with no value for it land in one named row, last, rather than being dropped: grouping by handler and hiding the unassigned work turns a board into a picture of what is already somebody's problem.

dueRule.description: Marks late cards. A card whose date is before today gets an error edge and the label 'Overdue'; one due within `soonDays` gets 'Due soon'. Omitted, no card is marked.

headerPill.description: A pill in a detail page header, rendered through CnStatusBadge from one field of the record. Nothing renders while the field is empty.

field.description: Dot-path to the value on the record.

colorMap.description: Raw value to badge variant. Keys are matched ignoring case.

labels.description: Raw value to the i18n key / text to show. A value without an entry is shown as is.

variant.description: Badge variant for a value `colorMap` does not name.

dueRule.description: How a surface decides that a dated item is late. One shape for boards and lists, so a list and its board agree. A date before today is overdue. Days are whole calendar days in the reader's own timezone.

field.description: Dot-path to the due date on the row.

soonDays.description: How many days ahead still counts as due soon. 0 marks only today.

variantWhen.description: The full rule list, in the shape a table's date cell uses, for a board that needs more than `soonDays`. Compared against the calendar days until the date (0 is today, negative is past); first match wins. `error` marks the card overdue, `warning` due soon. When set, `soonDays` is ignored.

dateAxisView.description: The date-axis view of this list: rows on a time scale, overlaps visible. Index pages only, and only offered when `viewModes` also lists `dateAxis`. IT HIDES NOTHING AND RESCHEDULES NOTHING: overlapping bars get their own track so the lane grows taller rather than losing a bar, rows with no usable dates go to a visible unplanned lane, and the only gesture is opening a row. A view that moved a bar on drag would be changing statutory dates from a picture.

startField.description: Where a row's start is. Required: a bar needs both ends, and a row missing one is unplanned rather than drawn.

endField.description: Where a row's end is. Required, for the same reason.

laneField.description: What to put in a lane together, usually the person the work is on. Omitted, everything shares one lane.

labelField.description: The field a bar is named by, on screen and in its accessible name. A bar positioned by percentage says nothing at all to a reader who cannot see it.

personalisation.description: The app's own defaults for the per-user options CnPersonalPreferences renders. The values a person chooses are stored in their Nextcloud preferences, never here; this block is only the bottom layer of the app default, administered value, personal value order.

enabled.description: Whether the personal layer applies at all. An administrator setting this false collapses it: the options render as unavailable with the reason, rather than being silently ignored.

disabledReason.description: What to tell a person when the personal layer is off. Shown beside the unavailable options.

landingPage.description: Page id the app opens on when a person has chosen nothing.

dateDisplay.description: How dates read by default. A relative date always carries its absolute date in the accessible name and the tooltip, because a term read as '3 dagen geleden' hides the date the term runs to.

rememberLastView.description: Whether each list reopens in the view mode that person last used on it.

pinnedMenu.description: Menu ids pinned to the top of the navigation by default. A person may reorder and repin their own.

primaryAction.description: A primary action declared on either a pages[] entry (active-page scoped) or nav.primaryAction (app-wide default). Rendered above the menu list as an NcAppNavigationNew button.

id.description: Stable identifier for this action.

label.description: i18n translation key / text for the button.

icon.description: MDI icon name (e.g. 'Plus'). Defaults to 'Plus' when omitted.

route.description: Named vue-router route to navigate to on click.

href.description: External URL opened in a new tab on click.

payload.description: Free-form payload echoed back to the host inside the @primary-action-click event.

action.description: A page action to run on click (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps): CnAppNav then renders the button through CnActionButtons, so `type: "open-form"` (with `register` + `schema`) opens the create dialog without a create page, `navigate` pushes a route, `api-call` calls an endpoint. Drawn as one solid full-width primary button. `route` / `href` on the primary action itself are ignored while `action` is set.

solid.description: Draw the primary action as a solid, full-width primary button whatever its form (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps). Default: a link action is already a primary button; a plain one is NcAppNavigationNew.

permission.description: Permission the reader must hold for the action to render, checked like `menuItem.permission` (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps).

visibleIf.description: Display condition evaluated at render time, like `menuItem.visibleIf` (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps). A gated-out page-scoped action falls back to `nav.primaryAction`.

menuItem.description: A top-level navigation entry. May contain one level of nested children.

id.description: Unique identifier for this menu entry. Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed — this is a router invariant.

label.description: i18n translation key resolved by the consuming app's t() function at render time.

translateLabel.description: Whether CnAppNav runs `label` through the translate function. Set false for a user-authored title (e.g. a catalog name) that must render as written even when it equals a translation key such as 'Search'. Rendered as text either way, never as HTML.

icon.description: CSS class for the icon (e.g. 'icon-checkmark') or MDI component name.

route.description: Vue-router route name (matches a pages[].id) that this entry navigates to. Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed — this is a router invariant.

query.description: Optional vue-router query parameters merged into the target route link (e.g. a filter like { caseType: '<uuid>' }). Deep-links a nav entry to a pre-filtered index page.

params.description: Optional vue-router route params for a parameterised route (e.g. { catalogSlug: 'news' } for a page at '/catalogs/:catalogSlug'). String values must be non-empty. CnAppNav links to { name: route, params, query }. The entry is active only while every declared param equals the current route's param (compared as strings), so sibling entries on one route that differ in params are never marked together. On pages whose path sits below its page path with these params filled in, it is active too: by the same params check when those routes carry the same param names, otherwise as the one entry marked below its route.

order.description: Display order in the menu. Items without an order render last.

permission.description: Permission string the user must hold for this entry to render.

section.description: Where the entry renders inside CnAppNav. 'main' (default) places it in the top list. 'footer' pins the entry to the bottom as a flat item above the settings foldout. 'settings' places it inside the NcAppNavigationSettings gear-icon foldout. 'integrations' renders the entry NOT in the navigation at all but in the Integrations section at the bottom of the per-user settings modal — the destination for links that leave this app for another (ADR-110). An 'integrations' entry MUST be clickable (href); a group with children is meaningless there.

type.description: Render kind. 'item' (default) renders a clickable NcAppNavigationItem. 'caption' renders an NcAppNavigationCaption section divider — only label, id, order, and section are honoured.

oneOf.description: A FILTERED count (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps): the total of this register and schema with `filter` applied (filter-value tokens such as `@me` and `@today` resolve at fetch time), fetched by CnAppRoot under the entry's own key so an index page's whole-schema total is untouched. Renders "My work 6" beside "All cases 48".

count.description: Counter badge in the entry's #counter slot. Positive integer renders as-is; 'auto' resolves from cnMenuCounts (populated by CnAppRoot from useObjectStore totals) for the entry's resolved index-type page (register + schema); an object `{ register, schema, filter? }` is the total of that filtered list.

pinned.description: Forwarded to NcAppNavigationItem's pinned prop. NC bottom-pins pinned items inside the parent list region.

open.description: Initial expansion state for a parent entry with children. When true and children[] is non-empty, the parent renders with :open="true" so children are visible on mount.

href.description: External URL. When set, the entry opens the URL in a new tab instead of dispatching a vue-router navigation.

action.description: Built-in action to invoke when the entry is clicked. Closed enum. 'admin-settings' opens the app-level admin-settings dialog (distinct from the per-user settings dialog). 'replay-walkthrough' re-runs the product walkthrough (ADR-043), optionally for a specific tourId.

tourId.description: Tour id for the 'replay-walkthrough' action (ADR-043); replays that tour from its first step. Omit to replay the default tour.

visibleIf.description: Optional display condition evaluated at render time.

dynamicSource.description: Optional dynamic source for populating nested menu items from a data endpoint. Carry-forward from v1.3.0.

children.description: Nested entries. Only one level of nesting is supported.

menuItemLeaf.description: A nested menu entry. Has no further children.

translateLabel.description: Same as menuItem.translateLabel: false renders `label` as written instead of translating it.

query.description: Optional vue-router query parameters merged into the target route link (e.g. a filter like { caseType: '<uuid>' }). Deep-links a nav entry to a pre-filtered index page.

params.description: Optional vue-router route params for a parameterised route; string values must be non-empty. Same contract as menuItem.params: part of the link, and the entry is active only while every declared param equals the current route's param.

dynamicSource.description: Dynamic source configuration for populating menu items from a backend endpoint. Carry-forward from v1.3.0 — identical shape to v1.

url.description: URL to fetch menu items from.

labelField.description: Property name in the response items to use as the menu entry label.

idField.description: Property name in the response items to use as the menu entry id.

routeField.description: Property name in the response items to use as the menu entry route.

linkCard.description: One card on a type='links' page: a link to another page of the app, or to a URL. Same vocabulary as menuItem and navCardEntry.

id.description: Unique within the page's cards.

label.description: i18n key / text of the card's title.

description.description: i18n key / one line under the title.

category.description: Key in config.categories naming the group this card sits in. A card without one, or with an unknown one, renders first under no caption.

route.description: Route name (a pages[].id), or a router path when it starts with '/'. Resolved through the router, so it works with and without /index.php. Mutually exclusive with href.

href.description: External URL, opened in a new tab. Mutually exclusive with route.

permission.description: Permission the user must hold for the card to render. Same rule as menuItem.permission.

visibleIf.description: Display condition, evaluated the way a menu entry's is.

navCardEntry.description: One card in a nav-card-grid built-in widget (ADR-044 §4 cards-collapse) — an arbitrary navigation link, not an OpenRegister object. Mirrors the menuItem/primaryAction vocabulary: id + label required, route/href are alternative navigation targets and mutually exclusive, count supports the same integer-or-"auto" shape as menuItem.count.

id.description: Unique identifier for this card within its widget's entries[] array.

label.description: i18n translation key / text rendered as the card's title.

description.description: Optional explanatory text rendered below the label, associated to the card via aria-describedby (never aria-label).

icon.description: MDI icon name (e.g. 'ChartLine'), resolved the same way as menuItem.icon.

route.description: Vue-router route name (matches a pages[].id) this card navigates to. Mutually exclusive with href.

href.description: External URL opened per the rendering component's target handling. Mutually exclusive with route.

count.description: Count badge on the card. Positive integer renders as-is; 'auto' resolves from cnMenuCounts (populated by CnAppRoot) for the card's resolved route page (register + schema), the same mechanism menuItem.count:"auto" uses.

order.description: Display order among sibling cards. Cards without an order render last.

permission.description: Permission string the user must hold for this card to render.

visibleIf.description: Optional display condition evaluated at render time.

allOf.description: route and href are mutually exclusive navigation targets — a card links either in-app or externally, never both.

widgetEntry.description: A uniform widget placement entry used on every page type in v2. Replaces the v1 widgetDef + layoutItem pair with a single shape. Its props/dataSource/filter string leaves are guarded against the closed sentinel vocabulary via the sentinelGuardedValue allOf. The cross-field constraint gridX + gridWidth <= 12 CANNOT be expressed in JSON Schema (arithmetic over sibling fields) — it is documented here and enforced at runtime by validateManifestV2() as a post-schema check. Failure message: "Widget '{widgetKey}' in slot '{slot}': gridX ({gridX}) + gridWidth ({gridWidth}) exceeds 12".

roles.description: Group ids that may see this widget. A DECLARATION THE HOST APP ENFORCES, not something this library evaluates: the check belongs on the read, where the figures are, because a widget hidden in the browser still had its data in the page payload (ADR-004). Pair it with `visibleWhen` pointing at an endpoint of the app's own, which IS evaluated here and collapses the cell when the fetch or the shape fails, so the declaration and the layout cannot disagree. Omitting it means every reader of the page sees the widget. Added because the key was expressible in the legacy `config.widgets[]` array, whose items are open, and refused here, so the same declaration validated on one page and was rejected on another.

visibleWhen.description: Render this widget only while the predicate holds. The same shape every other surface takes it in. It was already honoured at runtime for widgets (CnDashboardPage reads `def.visibleWhen`) and could not be declared in this shape, so a widget in the uniform entry had no way to express a visibility condition at all while one in the legacy array did.

requiredApp.description: Nextcloud app id this widget leans on — its data lives in that app's register, or its component comes from that app's integration leaf. When the app is absent the widget renders its normal chrome and a set-up state and issues NO request. Declared rather than inferred from content.register, because a register slug is not always the app id and a widget can depend on an app without querying it.

id.description: Optional stable, kebab-case identity for this widget entry. Used as the merge key under the `delta` merge mode (mergeManifestDelta keys widgets[] by id) so a stored delta can patch a single widget without resending the array. Omitting it keeps the entry valid; a delta simply cannot target it by key. Must be unique within a page's widgets[].

widgetKey.description: Registry key identifying the widget component. Resolved against the customComponents map passed to CnAppRoot at boot.

slot.description: Placement slot. Valid values: body, sidebar, header-actions, footer, modal (literals) or tab:<id> / section:<id> (pattern). Per-slot grid constraints are enforced via allOf/if-then below.

gridX.description: 0-based column start position. gridX + gridWidth MUST be <= 12 (enforced by post-schema check, not JSON Schema).

gridY.description: 0-based row start position. For header-actions slot, MUST be 0 (enforced by allOf/if-then).

gridWidth.description: Column span. For the default 12-column slots, 1-12. A page MAY widen a slot via config.slotColumns (up to the schema cap of 24); the real per-slot bound gridX + gridWidth <= resolvedColumns is enforced by the post-schema check, not JSON Schema. For sidebar slot, MUST be exactly 1 (enforced by allOf/if-then).

headerLink.description: One text link in the widget header's actions group, before the overflow menu (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps): "All deadlines", "To the board". A `route` (named page, optional `params` / `query`) is a router link, an `href` a plain anchor. The label is an i18n key. Rendered by CnWidgetWrapper; CnDashboardPage reads it off the layout entry or the widget definition.

showButtons.description: `false` drops the widget's footer links (its definition's `buttons`, e.g. a calendar's "More events"), for a placement whose card says enough without them (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-3).

sizeToContent.description: Opt-in: hand this placement's height to whatever it renders, so a widget that decides AT RUNTIME it has nothing to show costs no row. `true` sizes purely to content; an integer is a row minimum. It makes gridHeight advisory for this widget — right for anything whose height is whatever it turned out to be (a banner whose condition is false, a list that came back empty), wrong for anything with a deliberate size. Maps to CnDashboardGrid's per-item `sizeToContent`.

props.description: Optional widget-specific props passed at render time. Shape is widget-specific; not constrained here.

tabGroup.description: Optional: groups this widget into a named tab within the slot. Only meaningful for tab:* and section:* slots.

dataSource.description: Optional declarative data binding. Carry-forward from v1 widgetDef.dataSource — same shape.

dateChip.description: Opt-in (custom widgets only): when true AND the page's `dateRange.enabled` is true, the shared date-range chip renders in this widget's title bar (chart widgets with a `dataSource.bucket` get it automatically). Carry-forward from v1 layoutItem.dateChip — same semantics.

_note.description: Human-readable note. Optional on most widgets. REQUIRED when the containing page has type 'custom' — in that case this field must document why a standard page type was not feasible.

ncDashboard.description: Opt-in: also publish this placement as a widget on the native Nextcloud dashboard, alongside the app's own pages. An object rather than a boolean because a Nextcloud panel is a single narrow column with its own title, icon and link, none of which the grid placement carries. Presence of this key REQUIRES an `id` on the same entry (enforced in allOf below), and that id MUST be unique across the WHOLE manifest, not merely within its own page's widgets[] — Nextcloud's widget namespace is per app, so two pages both declaring id 'recent' derive one shared panel. Manifest-wide uniqueness is beyond JSON Schema; validateManifestV2 enforces it post-schema. Omitting the key leaves the widget visible only inside the app.

title.description: Panel title on the Nextcloud dashboard. Falls back to the widget's own title when omitted.

order.description: Initial ordering hint, passed through as IWidget::getOrder(). It decides where the panel first appears; once a user rearranges their own dashboard their arrangement wins, so this is a hint and never a guarantee.

link.description: In-app route the panel header links to, so a reader can open the page where the widget's full context lives. Written the way `pages[].route` is, e.g. '/reporting' — the host resolves it against its own app root with generateUrl() and never renders it bare. A scheme ('https:', and 'javascript:' above all) and a protocol-relative '//host' are both refused: the panel is rendered by Nextcloud's dashboard, outside this app's own pages, so a manifest is not a place to hand it an offsite destination.

allOf.description: ncDashboard requires a stable id. The host derives a permanent Nextcloud widget id from `id`, and Nextcloud stores each user's chosen widgets by that id in its own namespace, which no migration of this app can reach. A widget identified by array position would move onto a different widget whenever the array is reordered, silently changing what a user sees. `id`'s own pattern already refuses an empty string, so requiring the key is the whole of the rule expressible here; the manifest-wide uniqueness half lives in validateManifestV2.
sidebar slot: gridWidth MUST equal 1. The sidebar is a fixed-width panel; widgets always span the full width.
header-actions slot: gridY MUST equal 0. All header action widgets live in a single row.

object-table built-in widget: when props declares a `source` it must match the declarative self-fetch shape, an `endpointSource` (Wave 2) must match the shared endpoint binding (exactly one of source | endpointSource — post-schema check), and `actions` must be typed manifest actions (incl. type:'object-op'). Other props stay free-form (pass-through to CnDataTable).

endpointSource.description: Wave 2 (#91): endpoint-bound rows — the payload at responsePath must be an array; columns / formatters / rowRoute / actions apply unchanged on top. Exactly one of source | endpointSource (post-schema check).

actions.description: Declarative row/widget actions rendered by CnWidgetObjectTable. object-op patch/delete render per row; object-op create renders as a widget-scoped footer affordance.

rowClass.description: #91: declarative per-row CSS class rules compiled into CnDataTable's rowClass function. Each rule { when: { field, op?, value }, class } adds `class` to a row when the shared visibleWhen predicate holds against that row (field = dot-path into the row, op = eq|neq|gt|gte|lt|lte default eq, value = literal). Rules evaluate in order and every matching class is space-joined — so overdue / at-risk rows can be highlighted from the manifest. A host-supplied rowClass FUNCTION (runtime-only) still passes straight through.

when.description: The predicate evaluated against the row (shared visibleWhen grammar, LOCAL form).

value.description: Literal right-hand side of the comparison.

class.description: CSS class added to the row when `when` holds.

allOf.description: nav-card-grid built-in widget (ADR-044 §4 cards-collapse): props.entries is REQUIRED and each entry must match the navCardEntry shape. Unlike stats-block's optional entries[], nav-card-grid has no dataSource alternative — it renders arbitrary navigation links, not fetched data.

entries.description: One card per array entry, rendered by CnNavCardGrid.

allOf.description: stats-block built-in widget: when props declares `entries[]` each entry must match the statsBlockEntry shape. The exactly-one-of dataSource | props.entries constraint is a cross-field rule enforced by validateManifestV2() as a post-schema check (clear error message), not by JSON Schema.

entries.description: Multi-entry KPI sources — each entry renders one CnStatsBlock within the widget card. Mutually exclusive with a single dataSource.

allOf.description: banner built-in widget (CnBannerWidget, Wave 1): a declarative notice banner. props { variant, text, visibleWhen?, route? } — visibleWhen is a simple {endpoint|source, field?, op?, value} predicate evaluated at mount (fail-safe: hidden on fetch failure).

variant.description: Banner severity variant (NcNoteCard type). Default info.

text.description: Pre-translated banner text (required for the banner to render).

visibleWhen.description: Optional visibility condition: exactly one of `endpoint` (same-origin JSON URL) or `source` (OpenRegister object query). `field` is a dot-path into the response (source: into the first result; omit or use '@total' for the collection total). Fail-safe: the banner stays hidden until the predicate evaluates true.

source.description: OpenRegister object query; `filter` supports the shared @-token grammar.

field.description: Dot-path into the response ('@total' or omitted = collection total for a source).

value.description: Literal right-hand side of the comparison.

route.description: Optional click-through: a vue-router route NAME (string) or a full location object. Makes the banner text an accessible button.

layout.description: How the banner renders. `banner` (default) is the note card. `attention` is a card with a severity edge, a kicker, a title, a reason line and up to two actions.

kicker.description: Attention card: the small label above the title.

title.description: Attention card: the title. Falls back to `text`.

reason.description: Attention card: the line that says why this needs attention. `{value}` is replaced by the value visibleWhen read.

actions.description: Attention card: at most two actions. The first is the primary one unless an action sets `primary: true`.

id.description: Identifier passed with the `action` event of an action that has no route or href.

route.description: A vue-router route NAME (string) or a full location object.

href.description: An URL, used when there is no route.

primary.description: Render this action as the primary one.

allOf.description: audit-trail built-in widget (CnAuditTrailWidget, Wave 1): the object change-log card. All props are optional — register/schema/objectId normally arrive via the detail-page object-context merge; explicit props win.

register.description: OpenRegister register slug/id (context merge fallback when omitted).

schema.description: OpenRegister schema slug (context merge fallback when omitted).

objectId.description: The audited object's id (context merge fallback when omitted).

allOf.description: chart widget display passthrough (Wave 1): additive presentation keys forwarded verbatim to CnChartWidget by CnDashboardPage's dispatcher and the v2 grid. Other chart props stay free-form.

legendPosition.description: Legend placement override (empty/omitted keeps the automatic placement).

valueAxisBaseline.description: Value-axis baseline: 'auto' (the default — zero for bar/area, a bounded window for line/scatter), 'zero' (force a zero baseline), or 'fit' (let ApexCharts frame the data range, for a series living far from zero such as an SLA hovering 95–99%).

valueFormat.description: Named value formatter applied to the value axis + tooltip: 'currency' | 'currency-compact' | 'percent', or the object form { name, currency?, decimals? }.

currency.description: ISO-4217 code (EUR default; invalid codes fall back to EUR).

colorMap.description: Per-category colour map ({ categoryLabel: cssColor }) for pie/donut/radialBar slices and (distributed) bar categories.

emptyLabel.description: Empty-state message rendered instead of the chart when the resolved series contain no data points.

endpointSource.description: Wave 2 (#91): endpoint-bound series/labels — the shared endpoint transport plus the labelsPath / series[] {name, path} response mapping. Exactly one of dataSource | endpointSource (post-schema check).

allOf.description: header / text / divider on the v2 grid (Wave 1): the dashboard catalog's content-only presentation widgets reused as built-ins. Each takes a single `props.content` object with the same shape as its dashboard `content` blob.

content.description: The widget's content blob — header: { title, subtitle, backgroundImageUrl, overlayMode, height, cta, … }; text: { text, contentMode, fontSize, … }; divider: { style, lineColor, headingText, … }.

allOf.description: stat / delta catalog widgets on the v2 grid (Wave 2, #91): the KPI tiles take a `props.content` blob (same shape as their dashboard `content`). The endpoint-binding keys are typed here; the rest of the blob stays free-form (label, icon, format, source, …). Exactly one of content.source | content.endpointSource — a cross-field rule enforced by validateManifestV2() as a post-schema check (stats-block precedent), which also covers the legacy pages[].config.widgets[] placement.

endpointSource.description: Wave 2 (#91): endpoint-bound KPI value(s) — exactly one of source | endpointSource (post-schema check).

valueField.description: Dot-path into the endpoint payload for the displayed (current) value. Omitted = the payload itself.

previousField.description: Dot-path into the endpoint payload for the previous-period value — renders the trend sublabel (arrow + percent-vs-previous; the pipelinq previousPeriod contract).

deltaField.description: Dot-path into the endpoint payload for a SERVER-computed delta percent — wins over the client-side previousField computation.

goodDirection.description: Which trend direction tints green ('up' default; 'down' for cost-like KPIs). The delta widget's source.goodDirection still wins for the OpenRegister form.

variantWhen.description: First-match threshold styling rules for the stat tile — the matched rule's variant re-tints the value + icon circle, and its optional icon overrides content.icon.

op.description: Comparison operator against the resolved display value (numeric when both sides coerce; eq/neq fall back to string equality).

value.description: Literal right-hand side of the comparison.

variant.description: Colour variant applied on match ('default' keeps the configured colours). The component also accepts 'danger' as an alias of 'error' for doriath-migrated content.

icon.description: Optional MDI icon name overriding content.icon while this rule matches.

clickRoute.description: Whole-tile click-through: a vue-router route NAME (string) or full location object. Alias of content.route (route wins when both are set).

allOf.description: workspace-filter catalog widget (#91 Wave 3): a choice list whose selection writes into the page workspace context so sibling widgets refetch. The endpoint/OR-source binding keys of `props.content` are typed here; the rest stays free-form.

writes.description: The workspace context key the selection writes (`@workspace.<key>` or a bare `<key>`). Sibling widgets whose declarative source interpolates `@workspace.<key>` refetch on change.

allLabel.description: Optional leading 'All' option — writes the empty string so an optional sibling token (`@workspace.<key>?`) drops (unfiltered set).

options.description: Static options — each { value, label, count? } (or { id, name } / bare strings, normalised).

source.description: OpenRegister /grouped facet source { register, schema, groupBy, filter? } — each distinct value becomes an option with its object count.

endpointSource.description: App endpoint returning an array of { value, label, count? } options at responsePath.

allOf.description: kb-search catalog widget (#91 Wave 3): summary-driven knowledge-base search through a PLUGGABLE PROVIDER. The provider seam keys of `props.content` are typed here; the rest stays free-form.

provider.description: Provider registry key (default 'default' — the built-in endpoint search). An app registers bespoke providers (the xwiki proxy) on CnAppRoot's kbSearchProviders; the xwiki client stays app-side.

space.description: Provider-specific KB space filter (passed to provider.search).

tags.description: Provider-specific tag filter — a single tag or an array.

endpoint.description: The default provider's search endpoint (OpenRegister xWiki leaf by default).

queryParam.description: The default provider's query parameter name (default 'q').

bindTo.description: Workspace context key to auto-search on (default 'activeSummary').

minChars.description: Minimum characters before a search fires (default 3).

limit.description: Result cap passed to the provider (default 8).

externalOpen.description: Whether result links open in a new tab (defaults to the provider's own externalOpen flag).

unavailableFallback.description: Text shown when the provider rejects / is unavailable (replaces the default 'Knowledge base unavailable').

allOf.description: week-strip catalog widget (CnWeekStripWidget): the current week as day columns with the dated items under each day. Takes a `props.content` blob. Items come from an OpenRegister `source` (one request for the week, bucketed by `dateField`) or from static `items`.

days.description: 5 working days (default) or the whole week. The week starts on Monday.

source.description: OpenRegister object query; `filter` supports the shared @-token grammar.

limit.description: Cap on the records fetched for the week (default 100).

dateField.description: The field the items are bucketed by. Required with a source.

titleField.description: The field shown as the item title. Defaults to the object's display name.

itemRoute.description: Route name an item links to; the record id goes in params.id.

lateWhen.description: Rule on the number of days until the date that marks an item late. Default: before today ({ op: 'lt', value: 0 }).

lateField.description: A boolean field that marks a record late, whatever its date.

items.description: Static items, used when there is no source.

emptyText.description: Text of a day without items.

weekOffset.description: Whole weeks from the current one (1 = next week).

inset.description: Draw the strip inside the board's inset (16px above, 24px at the sides, 22px below) instead of from card edge to card edge (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-3). Theme hook --cn-widget-board-inset.

allOf.description: stacked-bar catalog widget (CnStackedBarWidget): one segmented bar with a legend that carries the label and count of every segment. Takes a `props.content` blob. Segments come from one grouped count request (`source.groupBy`) or from static `segments`.

source.description: OpenRegister grouped count; `filter` supports the shared @-token grammar.

groupBy.description: The field the records are counted per.

segments.description: Static segments, used when there is no source.

order.description: Group keys in the order they render. Unlisted groups follow; a listed key without records shows 0.

labels.description: The label of a group key.

inset.description: Draw the bar and legend inside the board's inset (16px above, 24px at the sides, 22px below) instead of from card edge to card edge (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-3). Theme hook --cn-widget-board-inset.

fieldWidget.description: A declarative widget-component slot used inside `form` / `detail` page config. Distinct from the top-level pages[].widgets[] grid placement (which carries widgetKey + grid coordinates). fieldWidget mounts a lib `Cn*` SFC inline as a form field or detail data slot; the renderer resolves `component` against the lib's exported component map, NOT the host-app customComponents registry. Carries serialisable `props` only — handler / function props must be wired via the host App's manifest-level mounts. Replaces the untyped `fieldWidgets[]` key relied on by pipelinq#415 (which rode through on additionalProperties: true). See ConductionNL/nextcloud-vue#314.

id.description: Unique identifier within the fieldWidgets[] array. Lower-camel-case-ish: must start with a lowercase letter and contain only letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. Used as the form field key / data binding key by CnFormPage / CnDetailPage.

component.description: Name of a lib component (e.g. CnMarkdownEditor, CnSchemaSelect). MUST be Cn-prefixed and resolved against the @conduction/nextcloud-vue exported component map. Host-app SFCs are not allowed here — those go through pages[].component on a type:'custom' page.

props.description: Serialisable props passed to the resolved component at render time. Shape is component-specific; not constrained here. Handler / function values are not supported through the manifest (the manifest is JSON).

_note.description: Optional human-readable note explaining the role of this declarative widget slot.

slotValue.description: Valid slot value. Either a literal slot name (body, sidebar, header-actions, footer, modal) or a tab:<id> / section:<id> pattern string.

oneOf.description: Named tab or section slot. Format: tab:<id> or section:<id> where <id> is at least one character.

dataSource.description: Declarative data binding for widgets. Forms: (a) shorthand {register, schema, filter?, aggregate: 'count'} — the lib builds a count query and resolves to {count}. (b) raw {graphql: {query, variables?, selectors}} — the lib issues the query and runs selectors. (c) #91 Wave 3 chart aggregation — `aggregate` as an OBJECT {groupBy, metric?: count|sum, sumField?, topN?, otherBucket?, labelResolve?} grouped over the schema's objects via OpenRegister's /grouped facet (client-side collection fallback), plus an optional sibling `drilldown` {route, filterParam}. Carry-forward from v1.3.0 widgetDef.dataSource.

filter.description: Shorthand: filter map inlined into the generated query.

aggregate.description: Shorthand aggregation. The STRING 'count' builds a GraphQL count query resolving to {count}. The OBJECT form (#91 Wave 3) is a chart-only categorical group-by served by OpenRegister's /grouped facet.

oneOf.description: #91 Wave 3 chart aggregation: group the schema's objects by `groupBy`, count (default) or sum `sumField`, keep the `topN` largest (sorted desc) and optionally fold the remainder into a translated 'Other' slice, resolving reference keys to labels/colours via `labelResolve`.

sumField.description: Numeric field summed when metric is 'sum' (required for sum).

topN.description: Keep the N largest groups (sorted by value desc).

otherBucket.description: Fold the post-topN remainder into a single translated 'Other' slice (sum of the rest). The Other bucket never drilldown-navigates.

labelResolve.description: Resolve reference (uuid) group keys to the referenced objects' display labels (and optional per-category colours) through the shared object store — the fkResolve pattern.

register.description: Register the reference points into (defaults to the dataSource register).

schema.description: Schema slug the reference points into.

labelField.description: Property used as the display label (default 'name').

colorField.description: Optional property read as a per-category CSS colour (feeds the chart's colorMap path).
