drilldown.description: #91 Wave 3 (chart only): a segment/bar click navigates to `route` with the clicked category's RAW key in the query ({ [filterParam]: rawKey }). A `/`-prefixed route is a path, otherwise a route name. Works with the OBJECT `aggregate` and the legacy `groupBy` forms; the folded 'Other' bucket never navigates.

route.description: Destination route name, or a path when it starts with '/'.

filterParam.description: Query-param name the clicked category's raw key is written to.

selectors.description: Map of result-prop name to dot-path selector.

action.description: A typed page action with a discriminator field. The type field determines behaviour: handler (registry function), open-modal (modal by id), open-page (named route), navigate (URL), object-op (declarative OpenRegister mutation via useObjectStore), export (opens the shared CnMassExportDialog export launcher), open-form (schema-driven create dialog — CnActionButtons), refresh (bumps the cn:page:refresh signal), api-call (POST/PUT an app endpoint + toast + refresh — CnActionButtons/dispatchAction), agent (run a governed hermiq agent), run-node (invoke one OpenRegister flow node against the page object, config collected via a dialog sourced from the node's own declared form — CnActionButtons/dispatchAction, or-flow-run-node; distinct from the UNRELATED setup-wizard step type of a similar name, 'run-action'), toggle (two-way state button — CnActionButtons only, NOT dispatchable). When type is omitted, it defaults to 'handler' (back-compatibility with v1.3.0 action declarations). The Ajv instance is compiled with useDefaults: true so the default is applied during validation.

id.description: Unique action identifier within the page's actions array.

label.description: i18n key resolved by the consuming app's t() function at render time.

type.description: Action behaviour discriminator. Defaults to 'handler' when omitted (back-compat with v1.3.0). handler: calls a registry function; open-modal: opens a modal by target id; open-page: navigates to a named route; navigate: navigates to a URL; object-op: dispatches a declarative mutation (patch | delete | create) of an OpenRegister object via the shared object store; export: opens the shared CnMassExportDialog export launcher configured via entities[]/formats[] — the confirm payload ({format, entity?}) routes to the action's `handler` in the manifest actions map (the app's export service does the download). open-form (#91 Wave 3): CnActionButtons opens a schema-driven create dialog (CnAdvancedFormDialog) for the action's register/schema, saves + toasts + refreshes + optionally navigates to onSuccessRoute. refresh (#91 Wave 3): bumps the page-level cn:page:refresh event-bus signal so every endpoint-bound widget refetches. api-call (#91 Wave 3): POST/PUT the token-interpolated url with payload/params (JSON body, payload resolves @-tokens recursively at any depth) + success/error toast + auto page-refresh (unless refresh:false); confirm gating is surface-consumed intent (object-op precedent); download:true requests a binary blob and triggers a browser file download instead (auto-refresh defaults to OFF in that mode). agent (hermiq#41): run a governed hermiq agent against the page object — POSTs { register, schema, objectId, resultField?, skill?, prompt? } to /apps/hermiq/api/agents/{agent}/run-on-object (object-RBAC-scoped; dispatches the governed AgentRunRequestedEvent). register/schema/objectId default to the page's @register/@schema/@objectId object context. A first-class companion to api-call (which remains the fallback for a bespoke body); hermiq is NOT hard-required — an app-level 404 surfaces a graceful 'agent runtime unavailable' toast. toggle (#91 Wave 3): a stateful two-way state button rendered by CnActionButtons (GET stateSource on mount, optimistic write on click) — NOT dispatchable through dispatchAction. object-op declares mutation INTENT only — authority is enforced server-side by OpenRegister RBAC (ADR-022/ADR-023); authorization-shaped fields have no client-side effect and are not accepted here.

op.description: object-op only: the mutation verb. patch merges `values` into the row's object (row-scoped); delete removes the row's object (row-scoped, ALWAYS confirm-gated); create adds a new object built from `values` against the widget's source register/schema (widget-scoped footer/header affordance). Required when type is 'object-op'.

values.description: object-op only: the verb's payload. For patch: the partial object merged over the row's object. For create: the new object's properties. Omitted for delete.

confirm.description: Confirm-gating (object-op + #91 Wave 3 api-call / open-form + agent): when true, the action presents a CnConfirmDialog before running (the dispatcher / CnActionButtons runs AFTER confirmation). object-op delete ALWAYS confirms regardless of this flag.

target.description: Destination for open-modal (modal id), open-page (route name), or navigate (URL). Ignored for handler type.

props.description: Additional props forwarded to the handler or modal.

createOverride.description: Registry handler name that owns the persist for an `open-form` action, replacing the default objectStore.saveObject. Resolved exactly as CnIndexPage resolves its own `createOverride` prop (a kind:'create-override' entry's `.handler`, a function-valued registry entry, or a function in the legacy customComponents map). Needed when the schema requires a field the create form cannot supply on its own — a server-minted foreign key, say — where a straight save would 400.

includeFields.description: open-form: the only fields the create dialog asks for. One schema often backs two surfaces, a detail page that edits all of it and a header button that collects what someone filing a new one types, and this is how the button says which it is. Omit for the whole schema.

excludeFields.description: open-form: fields the create dialog leaves out. Use it to drop a handful; use includeFields when it is easier to name what stays.

fieldOverrides.description: open-form: per-field overrides passed to fieldsFromSchema, keyed by field. Recognised keys include label, order, hidden, readOnly and widget.

advanced.description: open-form: open the properties-and-JSON table (CnAdvancedFormDialog) instead of the plain form. The plain form is the default because a header button is aimed at someone filing a record, not at inspecting its schema.

formTitle.description: open-form: overrides the create dialog's heading. Defaults to 'Create {schema title}'.

size.description: open-form: how wide the create dialog is, passed straight to NcDialog. Widen a form that asks enough questions to need scrolling; pair it with columns: 2.

columns.description: open-form: how many columns the fields flow into. 2 pairs them up, which halves the scrolling on a longer form. Textareas and JSON editors still span the full width, and the layout collapses to one column below 700px. Widen the dialog with size: 'large' as well, or two columns are merely two narrow ones.

handler.description: Registry key for type: 'handler'. Resolved across both registries passed to CnAppRoot: a v2 `registry` entry of `kind: 'handler'` exposing the function as `.handler` (or `.fn`), a directly function-valued registry entry, or a function-valued entry in the deprecated `customComponents` map. The same resolution serves actions[], bulkActions[] and headerActions[]. Also the built-in dispatch verb when paired with `route` (handler: 'navigate' → $router.push to `route`).

route.description: Destination route name for handler: 'navigate'. The dispatcher (manifestActionDispatch) calls $router.push({ name: route, params }). For row-level actions params include { id: row[rowKey] } automatically — do NOT restate it as params: { id: "{id}" }, though that placeholder does resolve (see `params`). Page-level header actions navigate without row context (e.g. a 'New X' action to a detail route).

icon.description: Optional icon for the action, rendered by CnActionsBar. Either an MDI icon name (e.g. 'TextBoxOutline') or a CSS icon class (e.g. 'icon-file').

entities.description: export only: selectable entity types offered by the export launcher (e.g. Leads / Requests). Optional — when absent the dialog shows only the format picker. Each entry needs an id + pre-translated label.

id.description: Entity id handed to the confirm handler.

formats.description: export only: the offered export formats — bare ids ('excel', 'csv', 'json' — lifted to {id, label} with an upper-cased label) or full {id, label} entries. Optional — the dialog's built-in Excel/CSV defaults apply when absent.

id.description: Format id handed to the confirm handler.

description.description: export only: pre-translated description shown above the export launcher's pickers.

url.description: api-call / toggle only: the app endpoint (POST/PUT). App-relative (routed through generateUrl) or absolute (http/https). May interpolate @objectId / @object.<field> / @workspace.<key> / @config.<key> tokens inline, as well as the literal {objectId} brace placeholder (unresolved tokens collapse to empty).

method.description: api-call: HTTP method (default POST). toggle writeUrl: default PUT.

payload.description: api-call only: the JSON request body — PREFERRED over `params`, and used instead of it when both are set. Values run the SAME token grammar as `params` (@me, @now, @today±Nd, @monthStart/@quarterStart/@yearStart, @objectId, @object.<field>, @workspace.<key>/@config.<key> with a trailing `?` marking a value OPTIONAL — dropped when unresolved) but resolve RECURSIVELY at ANY nesting depth, including arrays of objects — e.g. a Filinq document-generation body: { "dataRefs": [{ "register": "crm", "schema": "lead", "id": "@objectId" }] }. A required (non-`?`) token left unresolved anywhere in the tree BLOCKS the call (error toast) instead of sending the literal token string to the server.

params.description: Two distinct uses depending on the action's dispatch. (1) api-call / toggle: the JSON request body (legacy — prefer `payload` for anything with nested objects/arrays; ignored when `payload` is set). Values run the shared filter-token grammar ONE level deep (@me, @today±Nd, @workspace.<key>/@config.<key> with a trailing `?` for optional values dropped when unresolved; a required unresolved token skips the call). (2) handler: 'navigate' (index-page row actions, manifestActionDispatch): vue-router params merged OVER the default { id: row[rowKey] }. OMIT it for the ordinary 'open this row's detail page' action — the row id is already injected. String values run the `{field}` ROW-token grammar (NOT the @-token grammar): "{id}" resolves to row.id with its type preserved, "run-{id}" interpolates as text, and a brace-less "new" stays literal (that is what makes a 'New X' action navigate with { id: 'new' }). A token naming a field the row does not carry is dropped with a console.warn — so `id` falls back to the row id — instead of being pushed as a literal %7Bid%7D path segment.

download.description: api-call only: request the response as a binary blob (axios responseType 'blob') and trigger a browser file download instead of a JSON toast+refresh cycle. The filename is taken from the response's Content-Disposition header, else the token-resolved `filename`, else 'download.pdf'. The success toast still shows; unlike a normal api-call the page does NOT auto-refresh afterwards unless `refresh: true` is explicitly set.

filename.description: api-call `download: true` only: fallback filename used when the response carries no Content-Disposition header (falls back further to 'download.pdf'). Interpolates the same token grammar as `url` (@objectId, @object.<field>, @workspace.<key>, @config.<key>, {objectId}).

successMessage.description: api-call / open-form / agent / run-node / toggle: pre-translated success toast text (a library default applies when absent; agent default 'Run queued').

errorMessage.description: api-call / agent / run-node / toggle: pre-translated error toast text (falls back to the server's error/message, then a library default; an agent 404 with no structured body toasts 'agent runtime unavailable' instead).

refresh.description: api-call / agent / run-node / toggle: bump the page-level cn:page:refresh signal after a successful call (default true; set false to skip). EXCEPTION: for an api-call with download:true the default flips to false — a file download normally shouldn't also force-refetch every widget — set refresh:true explicitly to opt back in.

flowId.description: run-node only (REQUIRED): the published flow's uuid whose node this action invokes. A node's config and eligibility are properties of the flow it lives in (RN-3, OpenRegister's or-flow-run-node), so the manifest names which flow's instance to call rather than a bare node type — two flows could each carry the same node TYPE wired differently.

nodeId.description: run-node only (REQUIRED): the id of the node, within flowId's published graph, to invoke directly. POSTed to /api/flows/{flowId}/nodes/{nodeId}/run — refused (404) unless that node type has opted in to direct invocation (IFlowDirectlyInvokable).

subject.description: run-node only: the subject object the node acts on and is authorized against (OpenRegister object-RBAC — the caller needs update permission on it; the flow's own flow.run right is deliberately NOT what gates this). Typically @objectId; may interpolate the shared @-token grammar. An unresolved required token BLOCKS the call, matching agent's objectId.

agent.description: agent only (REQUIRED): the hermiq agent uuid to run against the page object. POSTed to /apps/hermiq/api/agents/{agent}/run-on-object (hermiq#41) — object-RBAC-scoped, dispatches the governed AgentRunRequestedEvent. May interpolate the shared @-token grammar (@objectId, @object.<field>, @workspace.<key>, @config.<key>).

skill.description: agent only: optional skill id folded into the governed run (interpolates the same @-token grammar as `agent`).

prompt.description: agent only: optional prompt handed to the governed run. Interpolates the shared @-token grammar inline (@objectId, @object.<field>, @workspace.<key>, @config.<key>) so it can be grounded on the page object — e.g. 'Summarise @object.title'.

resultField.description: agent only: the object field the agent's result is written back to (falls back to hermiq's default result field when absent).

objectId.description: agent only: the target object id. Defaults to the page object context's @objectId; an unresolved required @objectId BLOCKS the call (fail-closed) rather than sending a literal token. May be an explicit id or an @-token string.

register.description: open-form / agent / run-node: OpenRegister register slug. open-form: the create dialog's schema register. agent / run-node: the register the subject object belongs to — falls back to the page object context's @register.

schema.description: open-form / agent / run-node: OpenRegister schema slug. open-form: the create dialog fetches this schema and saves the new object against it. agent / run-node: the schema the subject object belongs to — falls back to the page object context's @schema.

onSuccessRoute.description: open-form only: optional post-save navigation target (#91). A bare route NAME (string) navigates with the saved object's id merged into the route params under `id` (harmless when the route has no `:id` segment — backward compatible). The object form { name, paramField?, objectParam? } names the id param (`paramField`, default `id`) and, when `objectParam` is set, also passes the whole saved object under that param key (for a props:true detail route to render without a refetch). The id is read from saved.id, then saved.uuid, then saved['@self'].id.

name.description: The vue-router route NAME pushed after a successful save.

paramField.description: Route param name populated from the saved object's id (default `id`).

objectParam.description: When set, the whole saved object is passed under this route param (props:true detail routes render without a refetch).

labelOn.description: toggle only: button label rendered while the state is ON (true). Falls back to `label`.

labelOff.description: toggle only: button label rendered while the state is OFF (false). Falls back to `label`.

stateSource.description: toggle only: the endpoint the initial state is read from on mount (the shared endpointSource shape — url + token-resolved params + responsePath). The `field` dot-path picks the boolean off the payload.

writeUrl.description: toggle only: the endpoint the flipped state is written to on click (interpolates the same tokens as `url`).

field.description: toggle only: the state field — read off the stateSource payload on mount AND sent (as the flipped boolean) in the write body under this key.

variant.description: CnActionButtons button variant (e.g. 'primary', 'secondary', 'error'). 'error' also styles the confirm dialog as destructive. A 'primary' action is never collapsed into CnActionButtons' overflow menu and consumes none of its `inline` slots: NcActions paints all of its inline actions with one shared variant, so a lone primary among them is not expressible.

children.description: Sub-actions, rendered by CnActionButtons as this action's OWN chevron dropdown beside its button — deliberately not folded into the page's single overflow menu, because NcActions cannot nest and a list that grows per record (app versions, say) would swamp it. Children take the same shape as any action, `visibleWhen` included, and an action carrying them consumes none of the `inline` slots. The parent itself still renders its own button beside the chevron (`type` defaults to 'handler' when omitted), so a parent meant only to group its children needs a `handler` that does something meaningful — an untyped, handler-less parent renders a button that dispatches to nothing.

childrenLabel.description: i18n key naming the `children` dropdown. Falls back to the parent action's own label, so the chevron is never announced unlabelled.

group.description: Detail page header actions only. i18n key / text naming the group this action sits in inside the overflow menu. Grouped actions render under a caption with this name, in first appearance order, after the ungrouped ones. Ignored on other surfaces.

adminOnly.description: Detail page header actions only. Shows the action to instance admins alone, in the last group of the overflow menu. Hides a control and nothing more: the endpoint behind the action still decides who may call it. Ignored on other surfaces.

visibleWhen.description: #91 Wave 3: an optional predicate gating whether the action renders — the shared banner shape ({ endpoint | source | field, op, value }). The `field`-only LOCAL form evaluates against the page object context (a detail action shown only in the right lifecycle state); endpoint / source forms fetch. Fail-safe: a broken predicate hides the action.

allOf.description: object-op actions MUST declare their mutation verb via `op`.
api-call actions MUST declare their endpoint via `url`.
open-form actions MUST declare the create schema via `schema`.
agent actions MUST declare the target agent uuid via `agent`.
toggle actions MUST declare their write endpoint via `writeUrl`.
run-node actions MUST declare which flow and which node within it (RN-3, or-flow-run-node) — a node's config and eligibility are properties of the flow it lives in, so neither can be inferred.

fieldValidation.description: manifest-form-logic: per-field validation rules for `type: 'form'` pages, enforced client-side by CnFormPage's validateFieldValue() before dispatch. Per-type semantics: string/password — required = non-empty after trim, min/max = string LENGTH, pattern tested against the value; number — required = finite number, min/max = numeric VALUE, pattern not applicable; boolean — required = value must be true (consent checkboxes), min/max/pattern not applicable; enum — required = a value is selected, min/max/pattern not applicable; json — required = non-null, min/max/pattern not applicable. Type-inapplicable rules are rejected by validateManifestV2() post-schema (pattern only on string/password; min/max only on string/password/number). `message` (i18n-able) overrides the built-in default message for whichever rule fails.

required.description: Whether the field must be filled. Default false. Per-type pass condition — see the fieldValidation description.

min.description: Minimum bound. String length for string/password fields, numeric value for number fields. MUST be <= max when both are set (validateManifestV2 post-schema check).

max.description: Maximum bound. String length for string/password fields, numeric value for number fields.

pattern.description: ECMAScript regex source tested against string/password values (implicit full-value test via new RegExp(pattern).test(value)). MUST compile — validateManifestV2() post-schema check runs `new RegExp(pattern)` in a try/catch.

message.description: i18n-able override message shown for ANY failing rule on this field, in place of the built-in translated default. Run through the page's `translate` prop, like `field.label`.

visibleWhen.description: #91 Wave 3: the shared visibility predicate (the Wave-1 banner shape). THREE modes: `endpoint` (GET a JSON endpoint, `field` dot-paths into the body), `source` (an OpenRegister { register, schema, filter? } query — `field` into the first result, or omit / use @total for the collection total), or LOCAL (neither endpoint nor source — `field` dot-paths into the caller's object context, e.g. a detail-page record). `op` defaults to eq. Evaluation is FAIL-SAFE (any error → hidden).

appInstalled.description: Nextcloud app id that must be installed and enabled for the guarded element to show. A PRECONDITION rather than a fourth mode: it is checked before anything else, and on its own it is the whole condition. Combined with endpoint/source/field it gates that mode too, so both must hold. It exists because the menu's `visibleIf` already spoke this word and `visibleWhen` did not, so the same manifest vocabulary meant two different things in two places. Use it on an action that writes into a sibling app, so an install without that app shows no button rather than a form that saves nowhere.

endpoint.description: A same-origin URL returning JSON; `field` is a dot-path into the body.

source.description: An OpenRegister object query { register, schema, filter? } (filter supports the shared @-token grammar). `field` dot-paths into the first result; omit it (or use @total) to compare the collection total.

field.description: Dot-path to the compared value — into the endpoint body, the source's first result, or (LOCAL mode) the caller's object context.

op.description: Comparison operator (default eq). eq/neq compare loosely-normalised primitives; ordering operators coerce both sides to Number. `empty` / `notEmpty` take no `value` and treat undefined, null, '' and an empty array alike — the one question eq cannot ask, because an unset field arrives in a shape that depends on the store and String(null) is the word 'null' rather than blank.

value.description: The right-hand side of the comparison, resolved through the shared @-token grammar so `@me` names the signed-in reader rather than a literal only the server knows. Omitted for `empty` / `notEmpty`.

all.description: Every listed condition must hold. Use it where a gate is more than one fact — a Claim button that is both 'not closed' and 'nobody holds it'. Each entry is a full visibleWhen and may compose again.

any.description: At least one listed condition must hold. Ignored when `all` is also present.

objectTableSource.description: Declarative self-fetch source for the object-table built-in widget (CnWidgetObjectTable). The widget resolves `filter` @-tokens (@me, @today, @today±Nd, @workspace.*, ?-optional suffix) with the shared resolveFilterTokens grammar just before fetching, and drives CnDataTable's existing self-fetch. `register` MAY carry an `@resolve:` sentinel — the widget passes it through unexpanded (resolution is the host loader's responsibility). Externally supplied `rows` always win over `source`.

register.description: OpenRegister register slug (or an `@resolve:<key>` sentinel, passed through unexpanded by the widget).

filter.description: Filter map (`{ field: value | value[] | { op: value | value[] } }`). Values may use the shared @-token grammar: `@me` (current user via @nextcloud/auth), `@now`, `@today`, relative-date arithmetic `@today±Nd` at day granularity (e.g. `@today-30d`, `@today+7d`), `@monthStart`/`@quarterStart`/`@yearStart`, `@objectId`/`@object.<field>` (detail context), `@workspace.<key>`/`@config.<key>` with a trailing `?` for optional clauses that drop when unresolved. IN-lists: an ARRAY value (directly, or via `{ in: [...] }`) matches any of its entries — tokens resolve item-by-item and the widget serializes the list as repeated `field[]` params (the shape OpenRegister parses).

order.description: Fetch ordering: field name to direction map (e.g. { "dueDate": "asc" }).

limit.description: Row cap. 0 (or omitted) shows all fetched rows; a positive value caps the rendered rows and enables the View-all footer when more rows exist.

extend.description: OpenRegister `_extend[]` values forwarded on the fetch (e.g. ["calculations"]) so read-time virtual/derived fields are hydrated and available as columns. Each entry is passed through verbatim.

endpointSource.description: Wave 2 (#91): ONE coherent endpoint data binding shared by the stat / delta / object-table widgets (the chart uses the extended $defs/chartEndpointSource). Reads an arbitrary app REST endpoint through the library's useEndpointSource engine: params pass the SAME @-token grammar widget filters use (@me, @today±Nd, @monthStart, @workspace.<key>/@config.<key> with a trailing `?` for optional values that drop when unresolved — a REQUIRED token that stays unresolved blocks the fetch), requests dedupe + short-TTL cache per (method, url, resolved params), and the widget refetches on cn:page:refresh / a matching cn:widget:refresh. Exactly ONE of the widget's OpenRegister source | endpointSource may be configured — a cross-field rule enforced by validateManifestV2() as a post-schema check (clear error message), matching the stats-block precedent.

url.description: Endpoint URL — app-relative (routed through generateUrl, e.g. '/apps/pipelinq/api/analytics/overview') or absolute (http/https, left untouched). May interpolate @page.<key> / @workspace.<key> / @config.<key> / @objectId / @object.<field> tokens inline; unresolved URL tokens collapse to an empty string.

method.description: HTTP method. GET (default) sends the resolved params as query parameters; POST sends them as the JSON body.

params.description: Request parameters. Values pass the shared filter-token grammar (resolveFilterTokens): @me, @now, @today, @today±Nd, @monthStart/@quarterStart/@yearStart, @objectId/@object.<field> (detail context), @workspace.<key>/@config.<key> with a trailing `?` for optional values (dropped when unresolved; e.g. `{ "period": "@workspace.datePreset?" }` rides the dashboard date-range pills). A required token that stays unresolved blocks the fetch until the page context provides it.

responsePath.description: Dot-path pluck of the response payload (e.g. 'summary', 'data.series'). Omitted = the whole response body.

chartEndpointSource.description: The chart widget's endpoint binding: the $defs/endpointSource transport plus the labels/series response mapping. The mapping keys live INSIDE this block (not as sibling props) because the chart's flat `series` / `labels` props already carry the static data. When the plucked payload is an ARRAY of points (e.g. pipelinq /api/analytics/trends → responsePath 'series'), labelsPath / series[].path are PER-ITEM field paths (labelsPath 'date', series [{ name: 'Leads', path: 'value' }]); when it is an OBJECT they point at parallel arrays. Pie-family charts flatten the FIRST mapped series into the flat value array ApexCharts expects. Exactly ONE of dataSource | endpointSource per chart widget (post-schema check).

url.description: Endpoint URL — app-relative (generateUrl) or absolute. Same token interpolation as $defs/endpointSource.

method.description: HTTP method. GET (default) sends params as query parameters; POST as the JSON body.

params.description: Request parameters — the shared filter-token grammar (see $defs/endpointSource.params). Params re-resolve and the chart refetches when the dashboard date range changes (the page publishes dateFrom / dateTo / datePreset into the workspace context).

responsePath.description: Dot-path pluck of the response payload. Omitted = the whole response body.

labelsPath.description: Labels/categories mapping: a per-item field path for an ARRAY payload ('date'), or the path of a parallel label array for an OBJECT payload ('labels').

series.description: Series mapping — one entry per rendered series.

name.description: Series display name (legend / tooltip). Defaults to the path.

path.description: Value mapping: a per-item field path for an ARRAY payload ('value'), or the path of a parallel number array for an OBJECT payload ('totals').

statsBlockEntry.description: One KPI entry inside a multi-entry stats-block widget (CnStatsBlockWidget `entries[]`). Carries the same source contract as a type:'stat' widget: register + schema + metric + token-resolved filter (@today / @me / @workspace.* and ?-optional clauses), plus per-entry presentation (title, variant, countLabel, format), an optional route deep link, and hideWhenZero. A money value names its currency with currencyField (the page object's field) or currency.

title.description: KPI title rendered by the inner CnStatsBlock.

register.description: OpenRegister register slug for this entry's count.

schema.description: OpenRegister schema slug for this entry's count.

metric.description: Aggregation metric for the REST /value aggregation (default 'count').

field.description: Field the metric aggregates over (metric-dependent; unused for count).

filter.description: Filter map with the shared @-token grammar (@today / @me / @workspace.<key>, trailing `?` for optional clauses).

route.description: Optional vue-router location for the KPI's deep link (renders the entry clickable).

variant.description: Color variant forwarded to the inner CnStatsBlock.

countLabel.description: Label displayed next to the count.

iconClass.description: Optional Nextcloud core icon class (icon-link, icon-mail, …) for the entry.

hideWhenZero.description: When true, the entry is omitted from the card when its resolved count is 0.

format.description: How the value is shown, as a type:'stat' widget's content.format: a style name, or { style, currency, currencyField, decimals, prefix, suffix }. Omitted, the plain localized count is shown. Numbers are formatted with Intl in the user's locale.

currency.description: ISO-4217 code, or a token such as @config.currency or @object.currency.

currencyField.description: Field of the detail page's object that holds the currency (dot-path allowed).

currency.description: Shorthand for format.currency: an ISO-4217 code, or a token such as @config.currency. Implies format 'currency'.

currencyField.description: Shorthand for format.currencyField: the field of the detail page's object that holds the currency, e.g. 'currency'. Implies format 'currency'. The currency is taken from the object, then currency, then the app's reporting currency (config currency), then EUR.

page.description: A v2 page definition. CnPageRenderer dispatches by type and matches by $route.name === page.id. All page types support a uniform widgets[] array for declarative slot placement. Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed in id, route, component, headerComponent, actionsComponent, or slots.* — those are router and registry invariants.

requiresApp.description: Soft dependency gating this WHOLE page. When the named Nextcloud app is not installed, the page renders the missing-dependency screen instead of its body. This is for the DEEP LINK: an entry gated by visibleIf.appInstalled is already hidden from the menu, so the remaining ways in are a bookmark, a shared URL, a redirect or an e2e spec, and those otherwise land on an empty page where 'not installed' looks the same as 'no data'. Gate a single WIDGET with visibleIf.appInstalled instead: a detail page may carry many widgets where only one needs the app, and that widget should hide while the page renders normally.

name.description: Human-readable app name shown on the screen; defaults to the id.

id.description: Vue-router route name. MUST be unique across pages[]. Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed.

route.description: Path pattern (e.g. '/decisions', '/decisions/:id'). Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed.

type.description: Page type. Closed enum of 18 supported types. 'links' mounts CnLinkCardsPage: a page of link cards grouped under captions, declared with config.categories + config.cards ($defs/linkCard). Use it for the pages a short menu leaves out; unlike 'reports' an app may have several. 'flow' opens ONE flow in the editor; the flow LIST is an ordinary 'index' with config.entitySource='flows'. 'flows' and 'flow-detail' are DEPRECATED aliases kept for migration — 'flows' predates named index sources and 'flow-detail' is the old name for 'flow'. 'roadmap' mounts CnFeaturesAndRoadmapPage (features + GitHub-issue-backed roadmap). 'search' mounts CnSearchPage (cross-schema query + facet sidebar + results list; consumers wire the actual search via @search). 'wiki' mounts CnWikiPage (manifest-declared markdown article + optional sidebar tree; MUST declare config.register + config.schema). 'flow' and the deprecated 'flow-detail' both mount CnFlowEditorPage (the shared node/edge canvas) and take config.app to scope to the owning app. A flow lives in OpenRegister's native flow store rather than a register/schema pair, so a single flow cannot be a 'detail' page — but the LIST is a plain 'index' once a named entitySource supplies it, which is why 'flows' is deprecated (ADR-110 Decision 4). 'custom' requires a _note field explaining why a standard type was not feasible.

title.description: i18n translation key for the page title.

permission.description: Optional permission identifier required to access this page.

component.description: For type='custom': name resolved against the app-provided customComponents registry. Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed.

headerComponent.description: Optional registry name for a component injected into the page's #header slot. Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed.

actionsComponent.description: Optional registry name for a component injected into the page's #actions slot. Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed.

sidebarComponent.description: Optional registry name for a component mounted as the default sidebar content for this page.

slots.description: Generic slot-override map. Each key is a slot name; each value is a registry component name. Sentinels (@resolve:*) are NOT allowed in values.

primaryAction.description: Active-page-scoped primary action rendered as an NcAppNavigationNew button above the menu list when the current route resolves to this page. Page-scoped declarations win over nav.primaryAction. Also the target of the detail page's skip link: a keyboard user tabs in, follows the link and lands on this action.

splitView.description: Index pages only. Opens a row beside the list rather than instead of it, at the sibling route <route>/split/:id that buildManifestRoutes() emits. Refused on any other page type.

board.description: Index pages only. The board view's configuration, handed to CnIndexPage as the `board` prop. The segment appears only when `viewModes` also lists `board`. Refused on any other page type.

dateAxis.description: Index pages only. The date-axis view's configuration, handed to CnIndexPage as the `dateAxis` prop. The segment appears only when `viewModes` also lists `dateAxis`. Refused on any other page type.

savedViewTree.description: Index pages only. Renders this page's saved views as a tree with labels, and declares the views that ship with the app. Refused on any other page type: a page with no saved-view dropdown has nothing to put in a tree.

manualOrder.description: Index pages only. Lets a person drag the rows into an order of their own, held per user and per list in their Nextcloud preferences and never written onto the records. Refused on any other page type.

tabInAddress.description: Detail pages only. Puts the active tab in the address as ?_tab=<id> so a link points at a tab of a record rather than at the record. The underscore prefix keeps it out of resolveQueryFilters(), which reads every other query key as a filter. Refused on any other page type.

referencePreview.description: Lets a reference on this page show a summary of the record it points at, on focus and on hover, without leaving the page. Rendered by CnReferencePreview.

widgets.description: Uniform widget placement array. Available on ALL page types in v2 (not just dashboard). Each entry specifies a widget key, slot, and grid coordinates. The cross-field constraint gridX + gridWidth <= 12 is enforced by validateManifestV2() post-schema check. Single-widget dashboards: a type:'dashboard' page with exactly one body widget covering the full 12×12 grid whose widgetKey resolves to a custom (non-library-built-in) registry component is REJECTED — see ADR-036 Decision 1 (single-widget dashboard anti-pattern). Use type:'custom' with component:'<widgetKey>' or split into N>1 widgets instead. Library built-in widget keys are exempt from the rule; the exempt set is LIBRARY_WIDGET_KEYS in src/utils/libraryWidgetKeys.js, which is held to set equality against the BUILT_IN_WIDGETS registry and the dashboard widget catalog by tests/utils/libraryWidgetKeys.spec.js. It is not restated here, because an out-of-date second copy of that list is the defect this replaced. Enforced by validateManifestV2() post-schema check.

actions.description: Typed page-level actions with a discriminator. Each action has a type field (handler | open-modal | open-page | navigate) that defaults to 'handler' when omitted.

config.description: Type-specific configuration. Shape varies by page type — see v1 schema for per-type config shapes (index, detail, dashboard, logs, settings, chat, files, form, map, custom). Config values under pages[].config may use the closed sentinel vocabulary (see $defs/sentinelTokenAny) — an out-of-vocabulary @-token FAILS validation via the sentinelGuardedValue allOf guard. Carry-forward from v1: register, schema, columns, actions, sidebar, sidebarProps, fields, sections, tabs, content, layout, widgets (dashboard only), cardComponent, columnGroups, etc.

entitySource.description: Name a registered NON-OBJECT entity collection for a type='index' page, instead of register+schema. Deliberately NOT called `source`: that key is already taken on page config and is polymorphic (a URL string in some manifests, an object with `params` in others), so reusing it would give one key two meanings and break six deployed shillinq pages. A flow definition is deliberately not an OpenRegister object, so an index had nothing to bind to and such lists became bespoke type='custom' pages. With a source the index loads the list itself. Takes precedence over register/schema; non-empty `objects` still wins over both. Registered sources live in src/composables/indexSources.js. `tasks` lists the viewer's task inbox from OpenRegister's flow-tasks read (cn-tasks-entity-source).

app.description: Scopes a named `entitySource` to one app (e.g. entitySource='flows' with app='dossiq' lists that app's flows).

contentField.description: type='wiki': property on the article object holding the markdown body. Defaults to 'body'. Maps to CnWikiPage `contentField` prop.

titleField.description: type='wiki': property on the article object holding the page title. Defaults to 'title'. Maps to CnWikiPage `titleField` prop.

idParam.description: type='wiki': $route.params key holding the article id. Defaults to 'id'. Maps to CnWikiPage `idParam` prop.

treeField.description: type='wiki': property on each sidebar tree node holding its child array. Defaults to 'children'. Maps to CnWikiPage `treeField` prop.

sidebarTitleField.description: type='wiki': property on each sidebar tree node holding its label. Defaults to `titleField`. Maps to CnWikiPage `sidebarTitleField` prop.

sidebarRegister.description: type='wiki': register slug for the sidebar tree. Defaults to `register`. Maps to CnWikiPage `sidebarRegister` prop.

sidebarSchema.description: type='wiki': schema slug providing the sidebar tree. When set AND `tree` is non-empty the sidebar renders. Maps to CnWikiPage `sidebarSchema` prop.

emptyText.description: type='wiki': empty-state heading shown when the article is null. Maps to CnWikiPage `emptyText` prop.

emptyDescription.description: type='wiki': empty-state description shown when the article is null. Maps to CnWikiPage `emptyDescription` prop.

emptyBodyText.description: type='wiki': empty-body heading shown when the article has no content. Maps to CnWikiPage `emptyBodyText` prop.

emptyBodyDescription.description: type='wiki': empty-body description shown when the article has no content. Maps to CnWikiPage `emptyBodyDescription` prop.

cardComponent.description: Registry name for a custom card component on index pages. Carry-forward from v1.3.0.

sidebar.description: Sidebar configuration. For index: object with enabled, show, columnGroups[], facets, etc. For detail: boolean or object with show, enabled, register, schema, tabs[]. Carry-forward from v1.3.0.

show.description: Whether to show the sidebar on this page.

columnGroups.description: Index sidebar column-visibility groups. Carry-forward from v1.3.0.

tabs.description: Settings tabs (for type='settings'). Carry-forward from v1.3.0.

sidebarTabs.description: Sidebar tabs declaration for type='detail' pages. Each entry is the human-authored source of truth for one tab — `id` + `label` (required), optional `icon`, `order`, `component`. Widgets bound to a tab carry `tabGroup: "<tab-id>"` on `slot:"sidebar"` entries; cross-reference is validated. The CLI manifest-migrate transform lifts `config.sidebarTabs[].widgets[]` into top-level `widgets[]` with `slot:"sidebar"` + `tabGroup`; tab entries declaring only a `component` are carried forward as residual sidebarTabs[]. See src/cli/transforms/liftSidebarTabWidgets.js.

id.description: Unique tab identifier within the page. Referenced from widgets[].tabGroup.

label.description: i18n key (or literal) for the tab label.

icon.description: Optional icon name (CSS class or MDI identifier) shown next to the label.

order.description: Optional sort key for tab ordering; lower values render first.

component.description: Optional registry name for a full-tab custom component. When set, the tab renders that component directly instead of the per-tab widgets[] grouping. Resolved against the customComponents registry.

_note.description: Optional human note (e.g. lib-gap reason for an undecomposable tab).

sections.description: Settings sections (for type='settings'). Carry-forward from v1.3.0.

fields.description: Form fields (for type='form'). Carry-forward from v1.3.0. manifest-form-logic adds two OPTIONAL typed properties — `visibleWhen` (reuses `$defs/visibleWhen`; LOCAL mode resolves `field` as a dot-path into the live form data) and `validation` (`$defs/fieldValidation`) — while every other carry-forward field shape (`key`, `label`, `type`, `enum`, `widget`, `help`, etc.) stays untyped via `additionalProperties: true` on the item.

visibleWhen.description: manifest-form-logic: optional conditional-visibility predicate. LOCAL mode (neither `endpoint` nor `source`) resolves `field` as a dot-path into the live form data — the first dot-segment MUST match a declared `config.fields[].key` (validateManifestV2 post-schema check). `endpoint` / `source` modes keep their existing fail-safe, evaluated-once-at-mount semantics.

validation.description: manifest-form-logic: optional per-field validation rules, enforced client-side by CnFormPage before dispatch. See `$defs/fieldValidation` for the per-type semantics table.

steps.description: manifest-form-logic: for type='form' pages, ordered multi-step wizard groups. Each entry is `{ id, title, description?, fields[] }` where `fields[]` is an ordered array of KEY REFERENCES into `config.fields[].key` — steps do not embed field objects (config.fields[] stays the single source of truth). Absent `steps` = single-step form, byte-for-byte the pre-change rendering. When present, validateManifestV2() post-schema requires: step ids unique within the page, every fields[] entry references a declared field key, and every declared field key appears in EXACTLY ONE step (complete partition — an unassigned field would silently never render; a doubly-assigned field would double-render).

items.description: One wizard step. `fields[]` order is the rendering order for that step's fields.

id.description: Unique step identifier within the page's `steps[]` array.

title.description: i18n key (or literal) for the step's title, shown in the step indicator.

description.description: Optional i18n key (or literal) for a short step description/subtitle.

fields.description: Ordered field KEYS (referencing `config.fields[].key`) rendered on this step.

fieldWidgets.description: Declarative widget-component slots for type='form' / type='detail' pages. Each entry mounts a lib `Cn*` SFC inline (e.g. CnMarkdownEditor as a markdown field, CnSchemaSelect as a relation picker). Distinct from top-level pages[].widgets[] which uses widgetKey + grid coordinates against the host customComponents registry. Carries serialisable props only. See $defs/fieldWidget and ConductionNL/nextcloud-vue#314.

columns.description: Table columns (for type='index' and type='logs'). Items may be strings (legacy shorthand) or column objects ({ key, label, sortable?, width?, formatter?, formatterOptions?, widget?, widgetProps?, format?, aggregate? }). `formatter` resolves against cnFormatters (built-ins incl. currency / conditionalPhrase — configured via `formatterOptions`); `widget` resolves against cnCellWidgets (built-ins incl. badge / fkResolve / link / avatar / date).

folderSidebar.description: type='index': the opt-in folder navigation pane (CnFolderSidebar) rendered left of the list. Selecting a folder filters the list by `filterField` (or `field`); "All" clears it. Only the per-scope list-layout keys are typed here; the pane's own keys (source, register, schema, idField, nameField, folders, allLabel, title, allowCreate, ...) stay free-form. Maps to CnIndexPage `folderSidebar`.

folders.description: Explicit folder list for source:'custom', and the place a folder declares its own list layout. Every other folder key stays free-form.

layout.description: Dashboard layout entries (for type='dashboard', legacy). Carry-forward from v1.

content.description: Declarative content items for dashboard (widget-ref items). Carry-forward from v1.

widgets.description: Legacy dashboard widgets array in config (for type='dashboard'). In v2, prefer top-level pages[].widgets[] with the uniform widgetEntry shape. This legacy config.widgets key remains for back-compat.

stageField.description: type='detail': dot-path to the field holding the record's stage. Read by `primaryActionByStage` and `nextStep`.

primaryActionByStage.description: type='detail': the page's primary button per stage. Keys are values of `stageField` (matched exactly first, then ignoring case). A value is an action in the header action shape, or the id of a `headerActions` entry, which then leaves the overflow menu. A stage without an entry falls back to the page's `primaryAction`.

quickActions.description: type='detail': at most three always visible buttons in the header, for the actions a handler uses on every record. An item is an action in the header action shape, or the id of a `headerActions` entry, which then leaves the overflow menu.

actionsMenu.description: type='detail': what the header's overflow menu itself shows. Omitted, the menu keeps Refresh and the three help links.

showRefresh.description: false removes Refresh from the menu.

showHelpLinks.description: false removes Request a feature, Report a bug and Documentation, for an app that offers them in its own help menu.

label.description: i18n key / text naming the menu, for example 'More'. Defaults to 'Actions'.

nextStep.description: type='detail': the 'what now' card above the body. For the record's stage it shows a short checklist next to the primary button. A stage without an entry shows no card. Rendered by CnNextStepCard.

field.description: Dot-path to the stage, when it differs from `stageField`.

title.description: i18n key / heading used by a stage that names none.
i18n key / heading of the card for this stage.

after.description: i18n key / one line under the button saying what follows.

checklist.description: What this stage still needs. An empty list shows no card.

label.description: i18n key / text of the item.

hint.description: i18n key / short note after the label, for example '2 of 5 done'.

doneField.description: Dot-path on the record. The item is done when it holds a value; a list counts when it is not empty.

doneWhen.description: A local visibleWhen condition ({ field, op, value } or { all | any }). The item is done when it is true. Wins over `doneField`.

done.description: A fixed state, for an item the record cannot answer.

typePill.description: type='detail': a pill above the title saying what kind of record this is.

statusPill.description: type='detail': a pill above the title saying where the record stands.

sideColumn.description: type='detail': a column of cards beside the body, for the record's facts. An item is a widget definition, or the id of a widget declared on the page. The column stacks under the body on a narrow page.

headerActions.description: Page-level header actions rendered inside CnActionsBar's overflow dropdown (between the built-in Refresh action and the `#action-items` slot). On a `type:'detail'` page the same entries render in the header's Actions menu, above the Request-a-feature / Report-a-bug / Documentation trio. Same shape as the row-level `actions[]` ($ref action), but handlers receive NO row context — they are page-level. Reserved ids (`refresh`, `import`, `export`, `copy`, `delete`) are dropped at render time to avoid shadowing built-ins. See manifest-icons-and-page-actions for the dispatch semantics.

bulkActions.description: Bulk actions rendered in the contextual selection strip that appears while rows are selected. Same shape as the row-level `actions[]` ($ref action), but the handler receives the SELECTION rather than a row: `{ actionId, selectedIds, count }`. For `type: "open-modal"` the selection is merged into the modal's props as `selectedIds` and `count`, so a manifest-declared modal component can act on the selection without the page hand-writing anything. Reserved ids (`copy`, `delete`) are dropped at render time: the strip already ships both as built-ins. Before this existed the strip had only a `#selection-actions` slot, which only a hand-written host component could fill — so a page declared in a manifest could carry row actions and header actions but never a bulk one.

actions.description: Declarative actions on a page. An object entry is governed ONLY by "an object carrying a non-empty label", deliberately: this key is polymorphic by page type (index rows dispatch $defs/action; detail pages also carry type='lifecycle-transition' entries), so one closed grammar here would reject working manifests. A label is what every dialect needs — CnRowActions renders an entry from its label and icon, so an entry without one became a full-height, clickable, EMPTY row in the overflow menu. An object is always an app action whatever its id: an id, when present, must be a string that does not start with 'builtin:', and the object may not set a 'builtin' key. On a type='index' page an entry may also be one of the placeholders "builtin:view", "builtin:edit", "builtin:copy" or "builtin:delete", each at most once, which puts that built-in row action at its position in the menu. A placeholder only places a built-in: config.actionToggles / the show*Action keys still decide whether it renders. Enabled built-ins the array does not place are appended after everything else in the order View, Edit, Copy, Delete. Any other string (a bare "edit", an unknown "builtin:archive") is refused, and placeholders are refused on every page type other than index.

rowIndicators.description: type='index': state indicators the page declares for its rows. Each entry names a `field` (a dotted path on the row), a condition (`equals`, `in`, or plain truthiness when neither is given), an `icon` (a CnIcon name) and a `text` (the text alternative, required). An entry without `text` does not render, because an icon with no text is colour and shape alone. The page declares which indicators exist; a record cannot add one the page has not declared. Maps to CnIndexPage `rowIndicators`.

rowIndicatorCap.description: type='index': how many declared indicators render on the row itself before the rest move into the row menu. Maps to CnIndexPage `rowIndicatorCap`.

quickEditFields.description: type='index': the fields a quick edit asks for, opened from a row without leaving the list. The page names them; a record cannot open a form on a field the page did not name. A field this caller may not write (see `writableField`) renders read-only rather than missing. Maps to CnIndexPage `quickEditFields`.

writableField.description: type='index': the dotted path where a record lists the fields this caller may write. A row carrying nothing there leaves every field the quick edit named editable; an empty list is a refusal and locks them all. Maps to CnIndexPage `writableField`.

viewTabs.description: type='index': saved view ids this page renders as tabs instead of as entries in the views control. A view appears in one place or the other, never both. An id naming a view that no longer exists produces no tab, rather than a tab that opens nothing. Maps to CnIndexPage `viewTabs`.

viewCounts.description: type='index': which saved views show how many records they match. `true` counts every saved view (tabs and the entries in the views control), an array counts only the view ids it lists. Off by default, so no count request is made. Quick filters opt in per entry with `showCount: true`. Maps to CnIndexPage `viewCounts`.

priorityField.description: type='index': the field carrying a record's DERIVED priority. The list reads the value and sorts on it; it never computes one. A record with no priority, or one outside `priorityLevels`, sorts after every ranked record in BOTH directions and stays in the list. Maps to CnIndexPage `priorityField`.

priorityLevels.description: type='index': the priority values in rank order, lowest first (e.g. ['low', 'medium', 'high']). Needed because a priority does not sort alphabetically into the order a person means. Maps to CnIndexPage `priorityLevels`.

listShortcuts.description: type='index': offer the list's keyboard shortcuts. Every shortcut is also listed in the command palette and on the help key, from one catalogue, because a shortcut nobody can find does not count. Maps to CnIndexPage `listShortcuts`.

rowActionField.description: type='index': the dotted path on each row where the server lists the actions this caller may run on that record (default '@self.actions'). A row's menu is then the intersection of what `config.actions` declares and what the server allows: an action the server allows but the page does not declare stays out, and an action the page declares but the server refuses stays out with its reason kept. A row carrying nothing at this path leaves the declaration standing. Maps to CnIndexPage `rowActionField`.

editOpensDetail.description: type='index': send the Edit row action to the record's detail page instead of opening the edit modal. OPT-IN — CnPageRenderer used to set this wherever a type='detail' page or config.rowRoute existed, and it no longer does: @edit-open is bound to the same navigation as a row click, so a routed Edit just repeats the row click (the split pane, or the detail page) and the form is no longer reachable from the list. Declare true per page when the modal cannot express the record. Maps to CnIndexPage `editOpensDetail`.

showEditAction.description: type='detail': show the header Edit button that opens the record's schema form. Set automatically by CnPageRenderer for every schema-bound detail page; declare false to make a detail page read-only. Maps to CnDetailPage `showEditAction`.

formSize.description: NcDialog size for the page's built-in Add/Edit form dialog (type='index' and type='detail'). A manifest `open-form` header action has always been able to ask for `large`; the built-in dialog could not, so the same app could have a roomy create form on one surface and a cramped one on another. Maps to CnIndexPage / CnDetailPage `formSize`.

formColumns.description: How many columns the page's built-in Add/Edit form flows its fields into. Pair 2 with formSize 'large', or the two columns are merely two narrow ones. CnFormDialog collapses back to one column below 700px, and a textarea or JSON editor spans both columns regardless. Maps to CnIndexPage / CnDetailPage `formColumns`.

excludeFields.description: Property names kept OUT of the page's built-in Add/Edit form dialog. Maps to CnIndexPage / CnDetailPage `excludeFields`.

includeFields.description: Property names the page's built-in Add/Edit form dialog shows, in this order — a whitelist, so anything absent is hidden regardless of excludeFields. Maps to CnIndexPage / CnDetailPage `includeFields`.

fieldOverrides.description: Per-field overrides merged over the schema-derived field descriptors in the page's built-in Add/Edit form dialog (e.g. `{ "description": { "widget": "textarea" } }`). Which widget a field renders as belongs to the surface, not to the schema. Maps to CnIndexPage / CnDetailPage `fieldOverrides`.

createDefaults.description: type='index': seed values for the page's built-in create dialog, never applied on edit. Resolves `@me`/`@now`/`@today` at any depth; `@object.*`/`@workspace.*`/`@config.*` need a context the page does not carry and pass through unchanged. Maps to CnIndexPage `createDefaults`.

createSuccessRoute.description: type='index': route opened after a successful create from the page's built-in Add dialog; the created object's id is merged into the params. Maps to CnIndexPage `createSuccessRoute`.

createSuccessMessage.description: type='index': toast shown after a successful create from the page's built-in Add dialog. Maps to CnIndexPage `createSuccessMessage`.

savedViewsScope.description: type='index': which pages share this page's saved views. By default a view is shared by every page over the same register and schema and by no other, because a view is filters over one schema's fields. Set this to share views across pages over different sources, or to keep two pages over one source apart. Written into the saved view's `query.scope`; views saved before scoping stay visible everywhere. Maps to CnIndexPage `savedViewsScope`.

splitCloseButton.description: type='index': whether the split pane draws its own close link. Set false when a `#split-pane` slot draws one from the slot's `close`. Maps to CnIndexPage `splitCloseButton`.

splitCloseLabel.description: type='index': accessible name and tooltip for the split pane's close button. Defaults to "Close". Maps to CnIndexPage `splitCloseLabel`.

showHeader.description: type='dashboard': `false` drops the header row (title, description, header actions, edit toggle) for a page that opens with its own heading, such as a greeting widget; the title stays as a visually hidden heading (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps). Maps to CnDashboardPage `showHeader`.

views.description: type='dashboard' | type='detail': views of the page, each its own widget grid behind one segmented control ("My work | My team") (view-switch-containers). The chosen view renders in a region below the page's own grid, drawn with the same grid and widgets; the page's own `widgets` and `layout` stay above it. The switch sits in the page header, or in a greeting header widget whose `content.views.options[]` carry `view` instead of `route`. The chosen view is in the address (`?view=<id>`) and in the user's preferences; the address wins. A view with nothing to draw shows `emptyText`, else a default sentence. On a detail page, views replace the automatic Data and Related body. Maps to CnDashboardPage / CnDetailPage `views`.

id.description: The view id, written to the address as `?view=<id>`.

label.description: The option label and the region's accessible name (through the app's translations).

icon.description: Optional MDI icon name, reserved for an icon-bearing switch.

emptyText.description: The sentence shown when the view has nothing to draw.

widgets.description: The view's widget definitions, the same shape as the page's `widgets`.

layout.description: The view's grid layout, the same shape as the page's `layout`.

defaultView.description: type='dashboard' | type='detail': the id of the view chosen when neither the address nor the user's stored choice names one; without it the first view (view-switch-containers). Maps to `defaultView`.

viewsLabel.description: type='dashboard' | type='detail': the accessible name of the page's view switch, e.g. "Whose work"; defaults to "View" (view-switch-containers). Maps to `viewsLabel`.

showWidgetActions.description: type='dashboard' and type='detail': `false` drops the overflow Actions menu from every widget that does not set `showActions` itself, for a dashboard whose widget headers carry a header link and nothing else (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-2), or a record page whose data cards carry none (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-3; a card with an Add action keeps it). Maps to CnDashboardPage / CnDetailPage `showWidgetActions`.

gridFloat.description: type='dashboard': `false` packs widgets upward (GridStack `float: false`), so a size-to-content widget that shrinks closes the gap under it instead of leaving an empty band (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-3). Maps to CnDashboardPage `gridFloat`.

showTitle.description: type='index': show the page header (icon, title, description) inline. Default false: the title renders visually hidden and the sidebar names the page. Maps to CnIndexPage `showTitle`.

countSubtitle.description: type='index': an i18n key for the description line with `{total}` replaced by the collection's total, e.g. "{total} open cases" (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps). Shown in place of `description` once a total is known. Maps to CnIndexPage `countSubtitle`.

showTitleIcon.description: type='index': `false` drops the icon before the page title, for a title that stands alone as the board draws it (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-3). Maps to CnIndexPage `showTitleIcon`.

showCount.description: type='index': `false` drops the actions bar's "Showing 20 of 258" line, for a page whose title line already gives the total through `countSubtitle` (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-3). Maps to CnIndexPage `showCount`.

headerButtons.description: type='index': buttons beside the page title, as the board's "Export" and "New case" (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-3). `action` is `add` (the Add flow; the label defaults to the Add label), `export` (the export leaf in `format`, else the export dialog), `import`, `refresh`, or the id of a `headerActions` entry. Shown only with `showTitle`; when they show, the actions bar drops its Views and Actions menus, and the Add button and Export menu when a button takes their action. Maps to CnIndexPage `headerButtons`.

showTypeEyebrow.description: type='detail': `false` drops the type eyebrow (the type label above the record name) once the record resolves, for a header that says the type in a pill instead (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps). Maps to CnDetailPage `showTypeEyebrow`.

breadcrumb.description: type='detail': a breadcrumb line above the header (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps): this crumb names the list the record belongs to (`route` + optional `params`, or `href`), the record's display name follows as the current crumb. Maps to CnDetailPage `breadcrumb`.

icon.description: Optional MDI icon name (e.g. `Home`) drawn as the first crumb instead of the label, which then becomes its accessible name (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-2). Without it the label shows as text.

currentField.description: A field of the record (dotted path, e.g. `identifier`) whose value is the current crumb instead of the display name; an empty value falls back to the display name (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-3).

separator.description: Text drawn between the crumbs (e.g. `/`) instead of the chevron (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-3).

headerCard.description: type='detail': draw the header (pills, title, actions) as a bordered card on the surface colour, as the board's case header (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-2). Maps to CnDetailPage `headerCard`.

headerWidget.description: type='detail': the id of a widget in `widgets` to render inside the header on its own row under the title, without a card of its own, e.g. the stages bars (zuiddrecht-pixel-gaps-2). The widget leaves the body grid. Maps to CnDetailPage `headerWidget`.

mapConfig.description: type='index': how rows are plotted when the Map view mode is available. Non-empty (and not excluded by an explicit viewModes) adds a Map segment to the view toggle. Maps to CnIndexPage `mapConfig`.

latField.description: Object (or `@self`) property path holding the marker's latitude. Dotted paths are supported, e.g. `@self.geo.lat`.

lngField.description: Object (or `@self`) property path holding the marker's longitude.

geoField.description: Alternative single property holding a GeoJSON Point geometry (`{ type: 'Point', coordinates: [lng, lat] }`). Takes precedence over latField/lngField when present and resolvable.

popupField.description: Object property rendered in the marker popup.

center.description: Fallback centre `[lat, lng]` when the filtered set has no plottable rows.

clustering.description: Whether coincident markers are grouped into a cluster that spiderfies on click. ON by default here — the opposite of CnMapWidget's own default — because an index map plots whatever the filter returns, and several rows at one address is the normal case: unclustered they land on identical pixels, the topmost takes every click and the rest are unreachable with nothing on screen saying they exist. Non-point geometry skips the cluster group, so areas are unaffected. Set false for the old behaviour.

quickFilterMaxVisible.description: type='index', chips mode: how many quickFilters render as pills before the rest move behind one more chip — a `⋯` pill that opens a panel of the hidden lenses, and that wears the label and the active fill of whichever one is on. 0 (the default) renders every lens, which wraps the actions bar onto a second line once a page declares more than a handful. The visible set is the FIRST n entries of quickFilters, so reorder that array to change which lenses stay out. Maps to CnIndexPage `quickFilterMaxVisible`.

actionToggles.description: Built-in action toggles for type='index' pages. Each key is sugar for the matching CnIndexPage prop — manifest authors can hide built-in mass actions / row actions / the Add button without writing a wrapper. Mirrors the CnIndexPage prop names. Explicit config.<key> wins over config.actionToggles.<key> (matches the readOnly precedence rule). Distinct from config.actions[] which is the typed row-actions array.

showAdd.description: Whether to show the Add button in the actions bar. Maps to CnIndexPage `showAdd`.

showFormDialog.description: Whether the built-in create / edit form dialog is enabled. Maps to CnIndexPage `showFormDialog`.

showViewAction.description: Whether to add a View action to row actions. Maps to CnIndexPage `showViewAction`.

showEditAction.description: Whether to add an Edit action to row actions. Maps to CnIndexPage `showEditAction`.

showCopyAction.description: Whether to add a Copy action to row actions. Maps to CnIndexPage `showCopyAction`.

showDeleteAction.description: Whether to add a Delete action to row actions. Maps to CnIndexPage `showDeleteAction`.

showMassImport.description: Whether to show the built-in mass Import action. Maps to CnIndexPage `showMassImport`.

showMassExport.description: Whether to show the built-in mass Export action. Maps to CnIndexPage `showMassExport`.

showMassCopy.description: Whether to show the built-in mass Copy button. Maps to CnIndexPage `showMassCopy`.

showMassDelete.description: Whether to show the built-in mass Delete button. Maps to CnIndexPage `showMassDelete`.

showViewToggle.description: Whether to show the table/cards view-mode toggle. Maps to CnIndexPage `showViewToggle`.

selectable.description: Whether rows are selectable (driving the mass-action surface). Maps to CnIndexPage `selectable`.

mode.description: Authoring / access mode. type='form': 'edit' loads from `data`, 'create' starts blank, 'public' shows the public-form success banner and skips auth-state requirements. type='detail': 'public' marks the route as unauthenticated (token-scoped reader pages — pair with a route-param token via the @route.<param> sentinel). Maps to CnFormPage / CnDetailPage `mode` prop.

subscribe.description: Collaborative-editing default for type='detail'. When true (the default) CnDetailPage calls `objectStore.subscribe(objectType, objectId)` on mount via `useObjectSubscription` and unsubscribes on unmount. Set to false for read-only or archive views. Mirrors the `subscribe` Boolean prop on CnDetailPage / CnObjectSidebar. See the `collaborative-editing-defaults` capability.

lock.description: Collaborative-editing default for type='detail'. When true (the default) the page wires `useObjectLock` so the locked-by-other banner renders when a remote lock is active. Explicit lock acquire/release on the edit toggle is the v2 follow-up; at v1 this flag controls whether read-side `lockState` is wired. Mirrors the `lock` Boolean prop on CnDetailPage / CnObjectSidebar.

sidebar.description: Per-page top-level sidebar visibility gate. Sibling of config, applies to every page type. show: boolean gates CnPageRenderer's #sidebar slot.

show.description: Whether the host App's #sidebar slot renders for this page. Defaults to true.

_note.description: Human-readable note. REQUIRED when type is 'custom' — must document why a standard page type was not feasible.

allOf.description: splitView, manualOrder, savedViewTree, board and dateAxis are index-page mechanics. splitView emits a second route beside an index route and mounts the detail pane inside CnIndexPage; manualOrder holds a per-user row order for a list. Declared on a detail, dashboard or custom page they would validate and then do nothing, which is the failure this branch refuses out loud (case-page-and-list-as-a-place).

The "builtin:<id>" placeholders in config.actions place CnIndexPage's built-in row actions, so only a type='index' page may use them. On every other page type config.actions holds objects only; a placeholder there would validate and then render nothing (row-action-builtin-placement).

tabInAddress puts the active tab of a record in the address. Only a detail page has a record and a tab strip, so the key is refused elsewhere rather than validating into a no-op (case-page-and-list-as-a-place).

type='wiki' (CnWikiPage) renders one manifest-declared markdown article. It MUST declare both config.register and config.schema as non-empty strings so the manifest stays the source of truth for which OpenRegister register/schema the article body is read from (manifest-wiki-page-type).

type='links' (CnLinkCardsPage) renders config.cards as link cards grouped by config.categories. It MUST declare a non-empty cards list, and every card is a $defs/linkCard, so a card that can go nowhere is refused here and not dropped in silence at render time (link-cards-page).

type='custom' requires _note documenting why decomposition into a standard page type was not feasible. Relaxed by ConductionNL/nextcloud-vue#315: when `component` matches the lib `Cn[A-Z]\w+` pattern, the component name already documents the choice and _note is optional. When `component` is absent or non-Cn (host-app SFC), _note remains required.

then.description: Lib-SFC custom page: component is self-documenting, _note is optional.

else.description: Host-app SFC custom page (or no component): _note is required to document why a standard page type was not feasible.

visibleIfCondition.description: A visibleIf condition block. Each key is either a reserved specialised condition (appInstalled) or a dot-separated path into manifest.runtime. Values are predicate expressions (scalar for eq shorthand, or operator object). All conditions are combined with implicit AND.

appInstalled.description: Nextcloud app id that MUST be installed and enabled for this entry to render.

deepLink.description: ADR-040 object deep-link descriptor. Maps an OR register+schema to an in-app URL template so other apps / the integration registry can resolve a deep link to an object. Permissive: extra keys are tolerated for forward-compatibility.

registerSlug.description: OR register slug the deep link targets.

schemaSlug.description: OR schema slug the deep link targets.

urlTemplate.description: In-app URL template; {uuid} (and other object placeholders) are substituted at resolve time.

displayName.description: Human-readable label for the linked object type.

adminSettingsEntry.description: One admin-only settings section rendered by CnAppRoot's generic admin NcAppSettingsDialog, sorted into the dialog by `order`. Exactly one of `type` (a built-in section) or `component` (a custom section resolved from the renderer registry) MUST be present.

id.description: Unique identifier for this admin-settings entry; also the rendered NcAppSettingsSection id.

label.description: i18n translation key (English source) resolved by the consuming app's t() function, shown as the section header.

type.description: Built-in admin-settings section. Closed enum. 'organisation-credentials' renders CnCredentials with scope="organisation" (the OpenRegister credential broker's organisation-scope pane). Mutually exclusive with `component`.

component.description: Registry key of a custom admin-settings section component, resolved from the CnAppRoot custom-components registry at render time. Mutually exclusive with `type`.

order.description: Sort order of this section within the admin dialog. Entries without an order render last, in array position.

permission.description: Optional permission string that further narrows visibility of this section WITHIN the already owner-gated admin dialog, reusing the existing per-item permission grammar. Narrow-only: it can never widen access to a caller who is not an owner of the app.

props.description: Props forwarded to a custom `component` entry. Ignored for built-in `type` entries.
